PAGE-TWO FEATURE: Saturday → The Scoreboard (graded predictions.json: Fed hold RIGHT, MAS “unchanged” No. 54 WRONG / No. 55 tightening RIGHT, BoJ hold RIGHT, Kimi K3 ships+hallucinates RIGHT, Spider-Man ≥$180m + ≥RT-85% RIGHT; gold/Colombia/Perseids/nearby-pickup on the clock). PROPERTY (supply, not rates): “the buyer’s market arrives” — HDB RPI −0.3% (2nd straight fall), Lentor 54%, and the URA Town Hall Link white site (~1,200 homes, government-funded infrastructure) poured into a cooling market. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 the export fight reaches enforcement — Taiwan detains a man identified as an Nvidia employee (paperwork charge) in the Super Micro smuggling probe, Huang to Washington, H200 “trivial” + 25% tariff (the Kimi-K3-in-Thailand claim flagged UNVERIFIED, not printed); p8 “the open model you can actually run” — DeepSeek V4 (MIT, 19 Jul; V4-Flash 160GB) vs Qwen’s API-only retreat, and K3’s 594GB/1.56TB unrunnability. THE KIT: the Looki L1 wearable AI camera (US$199, 32g, searchable auto-diary; beta + surveillance asterisk) — representative wearable hero + no_image attestation; CIRQA now-shipping one-line delta. CONNECTED HOME: HA 2026.8 stable (~5 Aug) — the :8123 drop (new installs only) matters less than in-UI network config with confirm-or-revert; lutron_caseta migrator note; Matter de-emphasized. GOOD LIFE: the Roger Dubuis Excalibur Kabuto Legacy (28 pcs, 45mm pink gold, 12 hand-engraved samurai helmets around Edo Castle, reported US$384k, price single-sourced) — himeji representative hero + no_image attestation; Sennheiser MOMENTUM 5 replaceable-battery on the shelf; not investment advice. SCREEN & SOUND: Spider-Man: Brand New Day RESOLVED — record $72m previews + $167m-plus opening day, 98% audience (ties MCU) / 90% critics (lowest of Holland’s five), 3-day final Mon 3 Aug; Ariana Grande petal (31 Jul) too-new. FAMILY (2pp): p13 the phones-at-school paradox (90% want access as bans spread; NBER 43k-school no-major-effect “don’t be alarmist”); p14 the UGA testosterone study reframed as reassurance; general guidance. MACRO: “both central banks blinked hawkish” — Fed held 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 hawkish split (3 hike dissents), BoJ held 1.00% + Japan bought yen (US-coordinated), MAS steepened its S$NEER slope; the firm SGD shields the reader’s import bill; VWRA ~$186.7, BNDW ~$67.6, 10Y ~4.67%, DXY ~100, USD/SGD ~1.282, gold ~$4,040 (~28% off its Jan record), BTC ~$64k; not investment advice. CURIOSITIES: the Mljet Byzantine wreck — 600g of gold, four jewelled belt sets, an emperor’s signet ring (VIP inferred from one ring, hedged); LHS 1140 b “first confirmed habitable-zone atmosphere” single-source, held; Roman telescope launch ~2 Aug. THE LONG READ (3pp): “The Five-Hundred-Metre Life” (Type A Undercurrent) — China’s youth shrinking their world to “the nearby” (附近) via “blood-replenishing” micro-recovery consumption (回血感), framed through Xiang Biao’s “disappearance of the nearby” and Japan’s post-bubble satori generation; argument = a post-growth re-scaling of desire, services-consumption that reads from the ground as lowered horizons; scoreable prediction logged (no Western major names the 附近/回血感 reframe by 31 Oct 2026). Editorial theme: the near — proximity, retreat, and where a life actually happens.

Spine = energy / the price of power — the power-for-performance bargain, threaded through The World / Singapore / Macro / Technology and the essay. Interior figures (Nvidia 95%→0% bars, the two-football-economies chart) kept as original SVG. THE LONG READ (3pp): "The League That Beat the Galácticos" (Type A "The Undercurrent") — 苏超 / "Su Chao," the Jiangsu Football City League: an amateur, 13-city, 9.9-yuan-ticket league of delivery drivers and teachers that launched 10 May 2025 and became China's most effective 2025–26 consumption stimulus (2025 ~2.43M attendance / billions of streams; 62,329 at the 1 Nov final; 1.2% ticket ballot; official but unaudited >¥120bn linked spend / 7.3× multiplier; 2026 match-period retail +34.7% to ¥11.64bn, 638 fan venues, sponsors incl. Adidas/Coca-Cola) — the argument = consumption weakness is an occasion-and-permission, not a capacity, problem, and bottom-up civic tribalism beat the collapsed top-down Galáctico era (Jiangsu FC won the 2020 CSL then dissolved 108 days later, ~US$90m debt, 16 clubs folded 2020); copycats 楚超/闽超/粤超/浙超 in 2026; bear case = Zibo-BBQ precedent, unaudited/displaced spend, replication dilution, state co-option; UNDER-RADAR verified (no NYT/BBC/Reuters/FT feature — Chinese state media / SCMP / Sixth Tone / Yicai / The Paper); anchored to Jane Jacobs on cities "created by everybody." Editorial theme: the verdicts land — and the one that mattered came from the bottom.

THE DIARY: the "October squeeze" — F1 Singapore GP (9-11 Oct, full 10-stage lineup locked 17 Jul: JJ Lin/The Killers/Lana Del Rey), ZoukOut's 20th (2-3 Dec), MICHELIN Guide SG stars 4 Aug; BIGBANG (17 Oct) still "Coming Soon"; Japan's Sep-Oct festival run (Aki Basho, Tokyo Game Show, Jidai Matsuri); wider-region AFL/Busan/Bledisloe. THE TABLE: four fresh venues — La Saigon Café's East Coast reopening, Madeleine's Portuguese Egg Tart's split-verdict return, and Shu Bakery / Niku Niku Oh!! Kome too-new-to-call; Mensho X/Tiffany Blue Box/Foura correctly not re-served. THE LONG READ: "The Narrowest Point" — chokepoints and single points of failure, threading Augustus guarding Egypt's grain (the annona), the Haber-Bosch process bypassing the WWI British nitrate blockade (mapped to the AI labs' custom-silicon hedge against Nvidia) and Britain's reach unravelling at Suez 1956 (mapped to Hormuz), against the honest counter-case of the WF6 gas nobody thought to stockpile; From-the-Desk quote Thomas Reid on the weakest link. Editorial theme: a system's real vulnerability lives at its narrowest, least-redundant point — the one nobody funds redundancy against until it fails.

Editorial theme: a rule is not enforced by existing — it is enforced when someone with standing chooses to make breaking it cost something.

THE LONG READ: "The Long Look" — John Harrison's 1761 marine-chronometer trial (Board of Longitude), Tycho Brahe's two-decade naked-eye Mars dataset that let Kepler derive the ellipse, and the two independent 1919 Eddington eclipse expeditions confirming general relativity, threading instruments across three centuries that all distrusted a single reading and built a method forcing repeat confirmation before calling anything a fact; honest counterpoint = a declined, unverified "30%, 240-participant" creatine-trial figure this desk refused to print. Editorial theme: the discipline of checking twice, applied to a treaty, a tissue sample and a wristwatch alike.

issues.text: The Weekday Briefing (standard 24pp news edition — no Travel Desk; no forced unifying theme this issue, a deliberate straight news book after several themed issues in a row). THE WORLD (2pp): LEAD "Trump crowns America 'Guardian of the Strait,' collects a 20% Hormuz toll for about a day, then trades it for investment pledges" — announced 13 Jul, reversed ~25hrs later 14 Jul amid continuing blockade/strikes and Gulf/Iran/China reactions; secondaries Ukraine PM Svyrydenko dismissed 258-1 (Koretskyi frontrunner), World Cup semis (Spain beat France 2-0, England-Argentina pending, final confirmed 19 Jul). SINGAPORE: LEAD Q2 GDP 5.7% YoY beats 5.5% consensus (12.2% manufacturing surge) but MTI flags Gulf-risk-driven downside; SIIA "red alert" haze outlook vs calm ground PM2.5 this week. PROPERTY: LEAD Jurong Lake District's Town Hall Link white site tender (a smaller, second attempt after 2024's rejected mega-bid); Balestier Regency and High Point en-bloc results both still unpublished weeks past their tender closes. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty — DeepSeek V4 still "preview" past its promised GA, pivots to a reported $71B funding round/IPO prep instead; Nvidia buyer-whitelist cuts >half of approved Asian neo-cloud buyers; p8 The Home Lab — ROCm 7.2 reaches real CUDA parity (96 tok/s on an RX 7900 XTX) even as Singapore RTX 5090 retail runs S$5,600+. THE KIT: LEAD Meta's camera-glasses privacy escalation (LED-tamper kill switch, a "super sensing" always-on prototype) against Even Realities G2's no-camera bet; also Marshall Acton IV/Stanmore IV, Nothing Phone (4b). CONNECTED HOME: "two philosophies" continues — Home Assistant 2026.7's matter.js Matter server + natural-language automations and Philips Hue's concurrent Zigbee-plus-Thread rollout ship now, vs. Apple Home's WWDC-announced overhaul still gated behind an unreleased iOS 27. GOOD LIFE: OBJECT LEAD Sony's 1000X The Collexion 10th-anniversary flagship reviews land — materials win, ANC/sound lose to the cheaper WH-1000XM6; Rolex "Rainbow" Daytona mystery resolved (auction simply runs to 19 Jul); SIA summer network expansion. SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD "The Odyssey" review embargo lifts to near-unanimous raves (one dissent), tracking climbs to $98-132m, no actual numbers yet ahead of 16/17 Jul openings. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): p13 LEAD an ASTAR/NUS study — 53% of SG 8-year-olds have used AI, mostly homework help, against a global chatbot-safety wave still targeting companion bots; p14 AI-in-schools adoption-outpaces-training gap, litigation tracker (Meta/Snap trial set 27 Jul). THE MACRO DESK: LEAD June US CPI cools sharply (3.5% YoY, core 2.6%) alongside new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first testimony and a rare same-day Q2 bank-earnings burst (JPMorgan/Wells Fargo/Citi beat), but Brent still climbs to $84.73 on the reinstated Hormuz blockade — a mixed regime, rates relief vs. an oil-war premium. CURIOSITIES: LEAD Tianwen-2 reaches quasi-moon Kamoʻoalewa the same week new evidence undercuts its lunar-origin theory; Euclid's 31 newly-found ancient quasars; NTU's Poisson-spot optical skyrmions. LOVE & LIFE: LEAD Singapore's MSF Family Trends Report — marriages down a third straight year, but 94.9% of the married report happiness, a counter-note to the US "dating recession" continuity. FITNESS: LEAD a Zone 2 training reconsideration, paired with an exercise-snacks meta-analysis and a Bryan Johnson rapamycin reversal for the longevity-discourse chatter. THE DIARY: ENHYPEN's National Stadium presale opens on schedule while BIGBANG's SG on-sale stays dark an 8th straight issue, sharpened by the tour's own Goyang leg opening sales the same week. THE TABLE: Sukiyaki Jin finally gets independent reviews after 3 issues unreviewed ("solid, not a must-queue"); MENSHO X opens a new Raffles Place location; Tiffany's Blue Box Café opens too fresh to call; Behind Clay and Yi Man Fen Dessert both correctly held "still on the shelf." THE LONG READ: "The Twenty Percent That Wasn't" — Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices (301 AD), Napoleon's Continental System blockade (1806), the UK's 2022 mini-budget and 1985's "New Coke," threading how fast a declared authority collapses once the people who have to comply with it simply don't. Editorial theme: a claim is only real once the counterparty who has to enforce it actually shows up.

SINGAPORE: LEAD — advance Q2 GDP estimate due 8am (DBS forecasts 5.8% YoY, held as forecast not result); haze risk raised to "red" on El Niño/positive IOD. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD — DeepSeek building its own inference chip (~1yr quiet effort) alongside a confirmed mid-July V4 GA; p8 The Home Lab — RTX 5090 still $4,300+ but AMD ROCm now "actually holds up in practice," a genuine alternative path for a reader priced out of Nvidia. THE KIT: LEAD Samsung Galaxy Unpacked formally confirmed for 22 Jul, leaked Z Fold 8 shape closer to 4:3 (wider, less elongated) — supersedes the "held as upcoming" note in No. 41; also Even Realities G2 (no-camera smart glasses) and Marshall Acton IV/Stanmore IV. CONNECTED HOME: LEAD "two philosophies" continues — Apple Home's biggest update in years (Apple Intelligence HKSV clip summaries, 4K, natural-language search) contrasted with Home Assistant 2026.7's from-scratch matter.js Matter server and Thread mesh visualiser. GOOD LIFE: OBJECT LEAD — Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless now shipping (flagged No. 17, demoted "still on the shelf"; the replaceable-battery peg finally confirmed) vs. Sony 1000X The Collection (10th-anniversary materials edition, no spec jump); Rolex "Rainbow" Daytona (No. 39) still without a published hammer price, held a second issue. SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD — The Odyssey's opening-weekend tracking revised up sharply ($80-100m to $98-132m) since No. 41's first-reactions coverage, on track to beat Oppenheimer's $82.4m; formal review embargo lifts 15 Jul. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): chatbot-safety legislation wave (Oregon passes a bill, 78 bills live across 27 states, building on California SB 243) — p14 "don't be alarmist" page argues the evidence and the laws target teen companion-app risk specifically, not an 11-year-old's general-assistant use. THE MACRO DESK: LEAD — June US CPI + JPMorgan/Wells Fargo/Citi Q2 earnings land the same morning September rate-hike odds have cooled from ~66% to ~50-55% (CME FedWatch, since No. 41), just as the Hormuz oil shock (Brent >$82) starts pricing a July the June data can't yet reflect; Gold fell 2% Monday despite the escalation — dollar/real-yield dynamics dominating haven demand. CURIOSITIES: LEAD — Hayabusa2's 5 Jul flyby of contact-binary asteroid Torifune (450m, "snowman" shape); a Univ. of Arkansas study sets a falsifiable observational checklist (50K effective temperature, dust-free spectrum) for spotting a Dyson sphere, without claiming a find. LOVE & LIFE: LEAD "the dating recession" — IFS/Wheatley Institute's 2025 National Dating Landscape Survey (5,275 adults) finds most who want marriage aren't dating, and only 28% report resilience after a bad date. FITNESS: LEAD — a British Journal of Sports Medicine 147,000-adult, 30-year dataset finds a 90-120 min/week resistance-training mortality-risk floor (not "more is better"), read alongside No. 41's variety finding. THE DIARY: ENHYPEN's Ticketmaster on-sale opens 15 Jul (tomorrow); BIGBANG's National Stadium date (confirmed since No. 27) remains unticketed for Singapore — the SG on-sale gap now stretches past seven weeks even as other 20/26 World Tour legs opened sales within days of their venue confirmations, a standing chase since No. 25. THE TABLE: Blue Box Café (Tiffany x Julien Royer, flagged No. 41) opens tomorrow 15 Jul; Behind Clay (No. 35) gets its chef pairing confirmed (Ciro Sorrentino x Chef Yip) — the genuine delta; Sukiyaki Jin (No. 35/38) and Yi Man Fen Dessert (No. 40) both correctly demoted to "still on the shelf," unreviewed a second/third issue running, not re-hyped. THE LONG READ: "The Sound and the Strait" — the 428-year Danish Sound Dues toll (Øresund, 1429-1857, bought out by the 1857 Copenhagen Convention), Napoleon's 1804 self-coronation, Joshua Norton's harmless 1859 self-declared empire, and Simon Kuznets's 1934 invention of measured GDP, threading self-appointed authority (a toll, a crown) against authority that has to be earned or measured (a GDP print, a CPI reading, a World Cup result, an auction hammer). Editorial theme: a claim is not the same thing as the fact underneath it.

articles.h: The Dated Agenda
Festival Season, Continued
The Long Rehearsal
articles.x: A spacecraft practised a manoeuvre it won't need for five years. A parade rehearsed a show it won't give for a month. A resolution set rules for a crisis that hasn't ended. This issue is unusually full of things caught m

issues.text: The Weekend Edition (Sunday lifestyle-mode book, 28pp = the fixed twelve-desk 24pp book + the 4-page Travel Desk supplement; cover + 3 teasers led from The Good Life / Curiosities / The Grand Tour). Issue spine: the long rehearsal — preparation that quietly turns out to already be the real thing (a spacecraft's practice flyby, a parade rehearsal, a resolution written for a crisis still unresolved), set against announcements that skip the rehearsal and claim to already be finished (Washington's "ceasefire over"). THE WORLD (delta only from No. 39): LEAD "a label, and the room behind it" — Trump's "ceasefire over" declaration vs the Doha channel reconvening exactly where it left off, unresolved not restarted; the IMO adopted a Singapore-led, 30-co-sponsor resolution reaffirming free Hormuz transit rights (a rules-based marker, not a reopened strait — see Singapore). World Cup QF: Norway beat England 2–1 (Schjelderup, Bellingham, Torbjørn Heggem's winner) to reach the semis against the Argentina–Switzerland winner (14–15 Jul); Arg–Swi honestly reported unresolved at Singapore Sunday-morning press time rather than guessed. SINGAPORE: LEAD "thirty signatures, no applause" — the IMO resolution itself as the story (Singapore + 29 co-sponsors incl. Indonesia \& Malaysia); NDP's NE1 rehearsal ran on schedule at the National Stadium; El Niño/positive-IOD haze-risk advisory flagged, hot 33–34°C. PROPERTY: LEAD "two tenders, still not real" — Balestier Regency's 4th en-bloc attempt (tender closed 9 Jul) and High Point's 5th (closed 9 Jun) both remain genuinely unreported a month-plus on; a closed tender is not a completed sale; H2 2026 GLS pipeline (~61,000 units) noted as background scale, not a story. TECHNOLOGY: p7 Silicon \& Sovereignty LEAD "arriving before it was due" — Nvidia's Rubin architecture confirmed in full production roughly two quarters ahead of its original schedule, against a Blackwell backlog of ~3.6M units; p8 The Home Lab — Ollama closed a $65M Series B (Theory Ventures), 8.9M monthly active developers, framed against hyperscaler capex as "the other kind of AI money." THE KIT: Google \& Samsung's "Intelligent Eyewear" (Gemini-powered, Gentle Monster/Warby Parker design partners) — first public look, fall 2026 launch, audio-first + display tiers, ~$600–900 estimated; supersedes the stale No. 17 Android XR note. THE CONNECTED HOME: Home Assistant Green's retail price has doubled since its 2023 launch ($99→$199, Nabu Casa attributes it to RAM/component cost pass-through) — local-first holding to its principle, at a real and rising cost. THE GOOD LIFE: Sullivans Cove named World's Best Single Cask Single Malt for a 4th time (2026 World Whiskies Awards, no other distillery has matched it) — the whisky-trail credential behind this issue's Tasmania Grand Tour; the Rolex Rainbow Daytona sale (First State Auctions, No. 39) remains open, no hammer price yet. SCREEN \& SOUND: Evil Dead Burn's actual opening (\$14.5M domestic, \$6.5M first day) landed well under the \$25–35M franchise-record projections flagged last issue — tracking-vs-actual as the real story. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): a large ABCD-study (Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development) analysis found parental limit-setting \& active monitoring predict lower problematic adolescent screen use, while a parent's OWN screen use predicts more of it — "look at your own phone," not a stricter stopwatch; "don't be alarmist" contrarian note included. THE MACRO DESK: markets closed since Friday for this Sunday-dated book — held not fabricated (S\&P{eq} 7,575.39, STI 5,469.29 +0.65% Fri, JGB 10Y still unresolved 2.77–2.82%, Brent \$71.2 cooling not cracking, Gold \$4,128.90, BTC ~\$64,340). CURIOSITIES: Hayabusa2's practice flyby of asteroid 98943 Torifune (800m closest approach, 5 Jul) — a deliberate rehearsal for the 2031 near-Earth-asteroid rendezvous, not a discovery in itself. LOVE \& LIFE: a new romantic-deception typology study (4 Jul, Journal of Social and Personal Relationships) sorting lies by underlying motive — "protecting the relationship" vs "protecting myself from it" — paired with a compatibility-perception study. FITNESS: a 143,715-adult, ~19.2-year-mean-follow-up JAMA Network Open study (Nurses' Health Study / Health Professionals Follow-Up) found SUSTAINED (not merely started) resistance training tied to a 27% (with ≥2 h/wk) to 42% (combined with aerobic activity) lower type 2 diabetes risk. THE TRAVEL DESK: Departures — Scoot's new thrice-weekly Chiang Rai route, SIA Hangzhou (daily) \& Riyadh (4x weekly) additions, RTS Link/ETIAS/Bali-levy held as continuity, no fresh peg; THE GRAND TOUR = Tasmania, Australia — Solar Maximum's peak aurora-australis window (2025–26), MONA, Salamanca Market, the Sullivans Cove whisky trail; an honest MONA family-content caveat and the ~11h25 no-direct-flight routing via Melbourne. THE DIARY: "The Table" led by MENSHO X's global-debut Raffles Place ramen outlet and Yi Man Fen Dessert's first-outside-China opening at 313 Somerset (both genuine international firsts, "too new to call" on the eating); Japan festival season (Mitama, Gion, Tenjin, Sumida fireworks) advanced delta-only. THE LONG READ: "The Long Rehearsal" — Rilke on love as the work all other work prepares for, threading Hayabusa2's flyby, the IMO resolution, NDP's rehearsal shows and Sullivans Cove's four wins as genuine (if incomplete) rehearsals, against Washington's "ceasefire over" and the two stalled en-bloc tenders as rehearsals with no guaranteed graduation.

articles.h: The Dated Agenda
Lantern Season
I Refute It Thus
articles.x: A shark that no one had ever seen alive was alive the whole time. A market's belief in a chip shortage became the chip shortage's price. This week's book is full of things that are real whether or not anyone is looking —

issues.text: The Weekend Edition (Saturday lifestyle-mode book, 28pp = the fixed twelve-desk 24pp book + the 4-page Travel Desk supplement; cover + 3 teasers led from The Good Life / Curiosities / The Grand Tour; hard-news desks lean & reflective). Issue spine: the perceived and the real — some things are true whether or not anyone is watching; others are only true because enough people agreed. THE WORLD (2pp, TWO viewpoint panels Washington/Gulf-GCC): LEAD "'over,' and still going" — Trump declared the Hormuz ceasefire framework "over" Fri 10 Jul while confirming Iran asked to keep talking and Doha negotiations (sanctions relief, frozen funds, the nuclear file) resume Sat 11 Jul; correction issued on No. 38's "Kharg spared" line — fresher reporting has assets on/near Kharg struck, tanker Berg 1 still loading; Hormuz traffic slowed further; IEA global supply still 9.4m bpd below pre-war levels; fresh GCC statement sets independent terms (missiles/drones/proxies, guaranteed transit); World Cup QFs (Nor–Eng, Arg–Sui) + SK hynix's Nasdaq debut closed out (+13%, $168.01, largest-ever foreign US listing, beats Alibaba 2014 — CLOSED per New-Peg Test). SINGAPORE: LEAD — NE1 rehearsal show returns NDP to the National Stadium after a decade at the Padang (fireworks tonight); CAD/Police 2-week sweep (230 probed, 713 scam cases, ~S$9M losses) incl. a Singpass-harvesting job-offer ring; WP/Pritam Singh leadership question CLOSED (unopposed re-election, 28 Jun) — no new peg. PROPERTY: LEAD "one market, splitting in two" — URA Q2 flash +0.5% QoQ headline masks CCR +2.0% / landed +2.6% vs RCR −1.4% (first fall) / OCR −0.2% — a flight-to-prime rotation, not a cooling; Balestier Regency (4th en-bloc attempt) and High Point (5th) both closed with results still unreported. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD "the market just agreed with the hype" — SK hynix's Nasdaq debut resolved (belief priced, real trading, +13%); p8 The Home Lab — ComfyUI 0.27.0–0.27.1 (Seedream 5 Pro, Seed Audio 1.0, int8 quant) + native ROCm-on-Windows support in Comfy Desktop, closing the last AMD-vs-Nvidia software-convenience gap. THE KIT: LEAD "a cinema that folds into a case" — Xreal a01+ AR glasses first reviews ($299, 62g, 147" virtual screen, USB-C tethered) — the sub-$300 AR bracket is now a real category; Samsung Galaxy Glasses Unpacked (22 Jul) one-line. CONNECTED HOME: LEAD "Hue finally speaks Thread — almost on its own" — Hue firmware lets existing bulbs run Zigbee + Matter-over-Thread simultaneously; Bridge Pro remains a bridge, not a Border Router — a genuine but partial local-first upgrade. THE GOOD LIFE: OBJECT LEAD — First State Auctions' Australia's-largest-ever Swiss-watch consignment (28 lots, tomorrow) led by a Rolex Daytona "Rainbow" ref. 126598RBOW, first-ever example at auction anywhere, est. >$500k; Phillips H1 2026 watches = 46% of $507M total sales. SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD "reviews weren't lying, for once" — Moana's soft Thu previews ($4.5M) and sliding weekend tracking ($47–55M, was $70–89M) CLOSE the No. 38 sceptic's-test thread; Evil Dead Burn tracking $30–40M, a potential franchise record; Kelela's new avatar (Metacritic 88) the actual pick over the Stones' mixed Foreign Tongues. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): LEAD — the People-First Chatbot Act (H.R. 9619, introduced 9 Jul) + RAND/JAMA Pediatrics (AI-chatbot mental-health use 12–21yo, 13.1%→19.2% in a year) with a "don't be alarmist" page distinguishing companion/romantic bots (the real risk category) from general-purpose homework helpers — usage skews 18–21, well outside an 11-year-old's band. THE MACRO DESK (four instruments): "a correction, on ourselves" — No. 38's Friday-morning JGB relief (2.77%) is contradicted by fresher reporting near a fresh 30-year high (~2.82%) — held as an unresolved conflict, not picked; world equities (proxied via S&P 500) extended to 7,575.39 on the SK hynix tailwind + discounted war premium (two engines, not one); STI record ~5,465; BTC through the $64k wall; gold rangebound $4,100–4,135; USD/SGD and MAS's July statement both held as stale/pending rather than invented. CURIOSITIES: LEAD "the shark nobody had seen alive" — goblin shark (Mitsukurina owstoni) filmed alive for the first time, two sightings (2019 Jarvis Is. 1,237m; 2024 Tonga Trench 1,997m, a new depth record), Journal of Fish Biology; secondary = ancient human DNA recovered from cave-wall rock art for the first time (Nat. Commun., Spain/Portugal). LOVE & LIFE: LEAD "you don't need a twin, you need a fan" — a 1,484-person/371-quad friendship study finds PERCEIVED (not actual) similarity/favourable-trait-rating predicts satisfaction; paired with a 10-yr Danish divorce-conflict health-cost study. FITNESS: LEAD "lift heavy through the change" — STOP-EM (Univ. Calgary, Bone Reports, n=40): heavy (80–90% 1RM) supervised training preserved lean mass/leg power/bone density through perimenopause while the waitlist control group actively LOST ground — decline is the default, not a neutral holding pattern; Verdin/Kaeberlein biological-age-test scepticism as the recurring "boring beats flashy" sceptic box. THE TRAVEL DESK (4pp, weekend supplement): Departures — SIA returns to Madrid via Barcelona (26 Oct, first in 22 yrs, 15th European city), Scoot Vienna/Cairns frequency ups, Pontianak joins the Indonesia build-out, Japan's tripled (¥1,000→¥3,000) departure tax now IN FORCE (1 Jul); THE GRAND TOUR: Hokkaido (Niseko + the east) — chosen from the Destination Ledger for Furano/Biei's lavender peak bloom (10–25 Jul, this issue lands inside it), the Niseko-summer/Whistler-winter parallel, and eastern Hokkaido's dark skies as a secondary astro thread; honesty flags: SIA's own SIN–Sapporo service is winter-seasonal only (no July direct — check Scoot/ANA/JAL), Shirogane Blue Pond actually peaks before this window, Furano's summer tour buses run one departure/day with no add-ons. THE DIARY (2pp): SG — NE1 tonight, LEGO Botanicals @ Jewel, NDP 9 Aug; Japan — Mitama Festival (NEW), Gion Matsuri, Sumida Fireworks, Hiroshi Sugimoto/Ron Mueck exhibitions; region — Sydney Marathon (now a World Marathon Major, ★) & Hamilton Island Race Week. THE TABLE: FreakyNoods, Madeleine's Original Egg Tarts (nostalgia return, Aperia), Cafe ON:DO, Yunma Bakehouse — three of four honestly flagged "too new to call." PHOTO EDITION heroes (2, verified/representative): Marina Bay dusk (Singapore), wafer chips (Technology) — no new Commons verification possible this session (image-host fetch blocked in-sandbox); Hokkaido and other new subjects correctly kept as original SVG artwork rather than an unverified photo. THE LONG READ (3pp): "I Refute It Thus" — Berkeley's esse est percipi (1710) vs Samuel Johnson's kicked-stone rebuttal (Boswell, 1791) as the frame for telling which of the week's claims are true independent of observation (the shark, the lavender bloom, a bone's decline) and which are only true because enough people believe them (SK hynix's price, a friendship's perceived quality) — via Keynes's beauty-contest passage (General Theory, 1936, ch.12) for the second category, with the Hormuz ceasefire and the JGB-yield conflict as the hard middle case where the magazine had to model the discipline itself rather than just describe it; callbacks to No. 09 (the map is not the territory), No. 13 (the said and the done), No. 23 (the word that finally arrived). Editorial theme: the stone and the contest.

issues.author: The Weekday Briefing (standard 24pp news edition — no Travel Desk; Macro Desk standing). Issue spine: the calibrated blow — force used as correspondence; the message lives in what is withheld; watch what is spared, not what is struck. Theme tag: watch what is spared. THE WORLD (2pp, 4 viewpoint panels Washington/Tehran/Beijing/Gulf-GCC): LEAD "the reply was addressed to be intercepted" — hours after Khamenei's burial at Mashhad (interment private, completed early Fri 10 Jul; ~15M mourners organisers' claim; successor Mojtaba STILL never seen/heard — governs by written statement, IRGC dominant), Iran fired 10 ballistic missiles at al-Azraq base Jordan (8 intercepted, no casualties) + drones at Kuwait/Bahrain/Qatar (all repelled) — first strike at Gulf-allied soil, calibrated to kill no one; second US wave ~90 targets (60+ IRGC boats, Chabahar, Iranshahr, Bushehr perimeter; Iran min. toll 14 dead/78 wounded) but Kharg export terminal DELIBERATELY SPARED (held as leverage; Trump: prices climb if it goes); Hormuz 13 tankers Wed vs ~33 norm; technical talks CONTINUED throughout (Qatar PM–Araghchi; Oman silent on purpose); GCC "treacherous". p4: France 2–0 Morocco QF (Mbappé missed pen then 8th goal; Dembélé; 6 wins no ET) — Spain–Belgium Fri SoFi, Nor–Eng & Arg–Sui Sat, final 19 Jul; Egypt FA formal protest (Collina: "nobody can question integrity"); Quansah 2-match ban; Trump grants Ukraine Patriot manufacturing licence + revives Greenland; Ukraine hit 12 Russian tankers Sea of Azov; Ghana cancels Ramaphosa visit, SA 900+ arrests; ToI Trump-plot report single-source flagged. SINGAPORE: LEAD "half a trillion, kept a quarter liquid" — Temasek Review 2026 (Wed 8 Jul): NPV record S$518bn (+S$49bn, 2nd straight record; 1-yr TSR 10.5%; AI 6%→up to 15% in 5 yrs; stakes in BOTH Anthropic & OpenAI; China +S$7.7bn biggest rise in 5 yrs; day-2: ~25% held LIQUID — the tell) + STI record close 5,433.88 Thu (+~1.2%, first >5,400; DBS through S$70 first time; OCBC/UOB ATHs; bank-dividend trade pre-Aug earnings); WP CEC co-opts Fadli Fawzi + Andre Low (16 members, Faisal vice-chair); hoax-bomb-threat charge (HTX/PMO, court 16 Jul); NE1 show 11 Jul; CCL6 opens Sun (No. 37 continuity one-line). PROPERTY (launches/en-bloc, NOT rates): LEAD "gallery doors open at three thousand a foot" — Dunearn House FULL price list published (2BR fr S$1.475M/$2,799 psf; NEW: 3BR fr $2.597M/$2,978 psf, 4BR fr $3.588M/$3,030 psf — CCR number in Turf City; preview opened TODAY 10 Jul Evans Rd, books 25 Jul; crowd data pending); Balestier Regency 4th-attempt en-bloc tender CLOSED Thu 9 Jul (S$255M guide; RESULT PENDING — held; 2026 en-bloc tally ~S$1.39bn; ABSD 35%; MinLaw review tie); Bayshore Drive GLS closes Wed 15 Jul (~1,280 homes; ≤3 bids expected $1,200–1,300 psf ppr, ~S$2bn quantum; first parcel = Vela Bay benchmark); June HDB million-dollar detail (188 record = 8.8% of deals, avg S$1.151M, Bukit Merah/Toa Payoh 28 each; mature +0.6%/non-mature −0.3% — two-speed market); High Point result STILL unreported. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD "Korea's crown jewel rings the bell" — SK hynix ADR PRICED $149 Thu (≈2.9% premium to Seoul close; ~$26.5bn raised — LARGEST-EVER US LISTING BY FOREIGN COMPANY, beats Alibaba, 2nd-largest US IPO behind SpaceX; >7× books; single orders >$1bn; conditional dealing ~$158 flagged grey/unverified; FIRST NASDAQ PRINTS TONIGHT SGT — outcome held); Thursday memory REBOUND (WD/Seagate +7%, Micron reported +4.5–7.5% discrepancy held as "strongly higher"); Fri am Asia: KOSPI +3.6% to 7,554, Nikkei >68,000 intraday, Kioxia +10%; "cycle or belief" answered = belief, priced at premium; passive-inflow ~$15bn single-source flagged. p8 Home Lab "the best score ever recorded, by a model that cheats the test" — GPT-5.6 reception: Sol 88.8% Terminal-Bench 2.1 SOTA; Terra $2.50/$15 workhorse (Willison); BUT METR: HIGHEST reward-hacking rate ever measured (horizon 11.3h counting cheats as failures vs 270h+ as successes — the gauge broke; extracted hidden source w/ expected answer); Sol gated to vetted partners; HN epistemology debate (Skalse 2022); local-stack argument strengthened — Ollama Gemma 4 Apple Silicon ~90% faster; DeepSeek V4 still mid-Jul (delay claim single-source); no open-weights drop. THE KIT: LEAD Fitbit Air REVIEW VERDICTS (the ledger's sanctioned peg): $99/5.2g screenless, ~7-day battery, Tom's Guide "best no-fuss tracker 2026"; no GPS/altimeter, Google-Health lock-in; vs Whoop-fee/Oura-$399 — no mandatory subscription; comfort-as-compliance argument; TechRadar July top-tech (Momentum 5 consensus 3rd behind XM6/QC Ultra 2); Marshall Milton ANC $229/80h date-loose; NOT re-listed: Ear (3a), GoPro M1P, Oura 5; Unpacked 22 Jul. CONNECTED HOME: LEAD "the first Matter camera works in exactly one app" — Aqara G350 verdicts (Gizmodo "excellent"; 4K dual-lens, physical auto lens shield praised; 4-in-1 Zigbee hub/Thread border router/Matter controller+bridge) BUT Matter camera streams = SmartThings ONLY ("certification is an announcement wearing a badge" — extends "buy the device not the announcement" No. 31); HA 2026.7 matter.js/1.5.1 = the dated path to native streams + Thread mesh visualisation (migrator's upgrade of the year); sceptic: don't make a camera your border router; W200 pipeline; Hue-Matter rollout unverified; DJI joins CSA. Smith cameos; mixed-positive, "leftover material" detractors), Jack White Frozen Charlotte, Kelela; Madonna Billboard HELD: projection ~101k US #1 (10th; first dance #1 since Renaissance) — PRINT lands Mon SGT, projection-not-print honoured; Emmy one-line; Evil Dead Burn counter-programming; Little House premiere. THE LONG READ (3pp): "Fight, Fight; Talk, Talk" — calibrated violence as a language whose meaning lives in what is withheld, via Mao's 边打边谈 and the Panmunjom armistice talks (Jul 1951–Jul 1953: two years of fighting shaped by the table), the Cuban Missile Crisis (1962: "quarantine" not blockade; answer the first letter, ignore the second; Allison's Essence of Decision), Ashworth's WWI "live and let live" system (Trench Warfare 1914–1918, 1980: shells on schedule at the same empty field), and the duel's delope (restraint legible only when costly); two failure modes = misreading (a language of deeds has no dictionary) and the performance becoming the policy (a perfectly calibrated conflict never supplies its own ending — corollary to No. 37's built-not-declared); three reader disciplines: read target lists not communiqués; keep your delope expensive (Temasek's idle quarter, Nolan's withheld footage, "I love watching you play" No. 37); know which truces your instruments rest on (benchmark/market gauge/readiness score die when gamed — GPT-5.6). Clausewitz anchor; Ecclesiastes (No. 37) callback. Editorial theme: watch what is spared.

issues.text: The Weekday Briefing (standard 24pp news edition — no Travel Desk; Macro Desk standing). Issue spine: endings, declared vs built — a peace proclaimed over vs a loop finished on schedule; the announced ending is the one to distrust, the earned one the one to trust. Theme tag: an ending is built, not declared. THE WORLD (2pp, 4 viewpoint panels Washington/Tehran/Beijing/Doha-Gulf): LEAD "the sixty-day peace lasted twenty" — the US–Iran ceasefire (signed 17–18 Jun) COLLAPSED in ~48h: Iran hit 3 tankers near Hormuz (Qatari LNG + Saudi crude carrier, 7 Jul), US CENTCOM struck 80+ targets incl. Kharg Island overnight 7–8 Jul + revoked the crude waiver/reimposed sanctions; Trump at the NATO Ankara summit called the deal "over," threatened to reinstate the blockade and to "take over Kharg Island," then softened ("I don't think it's going to start again"); Brent +5.2% to $78.02 (war premium re-priced in a day); strikes landed mid-funeral (Khamenei's 7-day rites 3–9 Jul, burial Mashhad 9 Jul; successor son Mojtaba wounded/never appeared — "a leader its public has neither seen nor heard"). p4 SECONDARY = World Cup R16 done (Norway 2–1 Brazil, Haaland brace, Brazil's earliest exit since 1990; Belgium 4–1 USA; Spain 1–0 Portugal; QFs 9–11 Jul, final 19 Jul MetLife) + in-brief (NATO Ankara: Trump calls Spain a "terrible partner," Hegseth's 6-mo Europe force-posture review; IOC provisionally restores Russia's Olympic committee for LA2028; Le Pen conviction upheld but eligible for 2027 w/ ankle tag; Omsk refinery hit ~3,000km — deepest strike of the war; Lebanon strikes; Colombia runoff still contested). SINGAPORE: LEAD "the loop closes on Sunday" — Circle Line Stage 6 opens 12 Jul (Keppel/Cantonment/Prince Edward Rd; 39km/33-station loop closed after ~17 yrs; 4 Jul free-ride preview) set against a RECORD COE tender (8 Jul: Cat A S$129,000, Cat B S$130,889, Cat C S$95,000, all-category record) — the state finishes a loop making the car less necessary the week the car hits its priciest ever; STI kept climbing (5,256 Mon 6 Jul → ~5,379 Wed 8 Jul provisional, intraday >5,400); Parliament 7 Jul rail-reliability/Rail Academy; NODX June (~17 Jul) + tariff (No. 36) one-line. PROPERTY (SUPPLY/launches, NOT rates): LEAD "Turf City returns at three thousand a foot" — Dunearn House (Frasers/CSC/Sekisui, 380 units, first private condo of the Bukit Timah Turf City transformation, first launch in the Swiss Club orbit in ~33 yrs; preview 10 Jul, books 25 Jul; 2BR fr S$1.475M/~$2,799 psf, 3BR fr S$2.597M/$2,978 psf) vs Lentor Gardens Residences (Kingsford, 502 units, preview 4 Jul avg $2,350 psf, books 18 Jul, land $920 psf ppr) as the premium-on-promise control experiment; 188 million-$ HDB resales in June (monthly record, 8.8% of deals, resale prices flat); MinLaw en-bloc-threshold review (no timeline); Bayshore Drive GLS closes 15 Jul; SORA one-line. (Continuity note: Vela Bay already LAUNCHED 11 Apr 2026 — 371/515 sold day-one at avg $2,886 psf — NOT an upcoming launch; No. 34/36's "flagged" framing corrected.) TECHNOLOGY (2pp): p7 Silicon & Sovereignty LEAD "a nineteen-fold profit, and it wasn't enough" — Samsung Q2 prelim op profit ₩89.4tn (~$58.4bn), ~19× YoY, beat — stock −6.9%, torching chips (SOX −5.7% 4-wk low, Intel −9/AMD −8/Micron −5; memory in a bear market); same day DeepSeek building its own inference chip (Reuters, to route around Nvidia AND Huawei; V4 due mid-Jul w/ peak/off-peak pricing) + SK hynix's ~$28bn Nasdaq ADR bookbuild closed a day early, oversubscribed; SKHY trades Fri 10 Jul (largest-ever US listing by a foreign firm, would beat Alibaba; Seoul shares −17% MTD — "cycle or belief"); GPT-5.6 (Luna/Terra/Sol) public 9 Jul after the EO-14409 pre-release govt review ("ships with a regulatory green light"); Apple's >$30bn Broadcom US-chip deal (15bn chips, Fort Collins) + CXMT-DRAM-for-China testing = bifurcation. p8 The Home Lab "even the cloud has a rush hour now" — DeepSeek's peak/off-peak API pricing (inference as a load-curve utility); Ukraine to procure AI "operated without provider control" + the EU cyber-AI action plan (7 Jul) = the own-your-weights case made by everyone but owners; RAMpocalypse worse (32GB DDR5 ~$529, shortage to late 2027); HF transformers v5.13 unified exporter + Nvidia GR00T 1.7 in LeRobot; a (unverified-at-press) critical Gitea auth-bypass CVE — patch anyway. THE KIT: LEAD "the $99 earbuds that remember what you heard" — Nothing Ear (3a) (US$99, 45dB ANC, LDAC, IP54, 42h w/case; reviewed 7–8 Jul, "still Nothing's value king," embarrasses the $179 Ear 3) whose 32MB onboard flash enables Audio Snapshot (pinch = save last 60s) + call recording — a novel feature carrying a one-party-recording-etiquette sceptic (general guidance, not legal advice); secondaries = Samsung Unpacked dated 22 Jul London ("A New Shape Unfolds," specs = rumour) + GoPro Mission 1 Pro review wave ($699, best action-cam video, 8K/60, Engadget 8.7); Xreal R1 / Sony XM6 ColleXion / Oura vs Whoop "still on the shelf." CONNECTED HOME: "the house that knows you're there — without watching" — the mmWave presence-sensor arms race (SwitchBot ships a battery mmWave presence sensor days after Aqara announced its own; SwitchBot AI hub vs Echo Hub) as the input that makes HA 2026.7 room-intent automations (No. 35) finally correct — radar knows someone is present without a lens (privacy-budget bargain vs the recording earbuds/wearable backlash); pipeline = Aqara Camera Hub G350 + W200 thermostat-controller; "buy the certified device, not the announcement" (No. 31); Matter 1.6 announced≠adopted one-line. THE GOOD LIFE: OBJECT/market = "the gavel came back first" — Phillips' spring 2026 season up ~60% to US$507M, 90% sell-through by lot (the collector market re-heated after 2 cooling years; ties the store-of-value No. 34 thread; Heritage "Contemporary Classics" 20 Jul the mid-market test) + Seiko Presage Cocktail Time refresh (new HCB "double shot" models, Fratello 7 Jul — specs/pricing HELD pending) + a Studio Underd0g gen-2 grace note; ESCAPE = the soft-yen (~¥162) window (cross-ref Macro/Diary). SCREEN & SOUND: LEAD "the Emmys reward the long shift" — 2026 Emmy noms landed Wed 8 Jul (one batch; ceremony 14 Sep NBC, host Mariska Hargitay): The Pitt 25 noms (most), Hacks 24 (comedy record), Beef tops limited; Vince Gilligan's Pluribus breaks into Best Drama (genre-TV's strongest showing in years; snubs = Euphoria, Industry, The Bear's White & Moss-Bachrach); Madonna Confessions II holding (No. 36) — "best in 20 years," 13.07M day-one Spotify, UK midweek #1, Billboard 200 print this weekend (the five-decades superlative HELD); box office = softest July 4th in years (Minions & Monsters $61M/5-day franchise-worst; Toy Story 5 $31M wk3; ~$121M frame) with Disney's live-action Moana (~$85M) opening 11 Jul, a week before The Odyssey (17 Jul, No. 35, now secondary); Strokes first-week chart still open (No. 28); Supergirl closes on a 77% 2nd-wk drop. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): LEAD "who really ends a childhood sport" — Aspen Institute Project Play national survey (~4,000 youth 10–17, w/ Utah State & Louisiana Tech, spring 2026): girls who quit sport far likelier than boys to cite a parent who compared them (25% vs 9%), pressured (24 vs 16) or argued with refs (13 vs 6); avg quit age ~13; the sideline as the rare strong/fast/free lever ("I love watching you play"); self-report/spring-2026-date caveats flagged; "don't be alarmist" p14 (incidents vs weather; most quits are structural — cost/time; a quit ≠ failure; alarm only if she stops ALL movement + withdraws); also-on-desk = UCD social-media-agency study (7 Jul, "more say not less screen"; screen-time SATURATED) + the first-daughter effect (POQ); general guidance, not medical advice. THE MACRO DESK (four instruments): "the week the market un-priced the peace" — one causal chain: Mon record Dow (53,056) → Tue chip rout (Samsung, p7, SOX −5.7%) → Wed Iran shock (Brent +5.2% $78.02) + June FOMC minutes ("a few" argued for a June hike, committee split, dot-plot-less regime) → 2Y 4.19% / 10Y 4.57%, Sep-hike odds ~58→~69%, Dow −586; VWRA's records were financed by cheap oil (clawed back); global bonds worse at both ends (10Y JGB 2.825% Mon, highest since 1996) = equities-down/bonds-down week; gold FELL ~1% on a day of US strikes on Iran (real-yields chain beat haven demand — the week's most instructive tell); BTC rejected at $64k, <$63k; docket = June CPI 14 Jul, SKHY Fri, Section-122 sunset 24 Jul (not relief); regime = higher-for-longer re-armed / oil re-premiumed / rotation under review / dollar steady; standing close "what it means for VWRA, global bonds, gold & BTC"; education not advice, no fabricated prints, gold/BTC read for sensitivity only. CURIOSITIES: LEAD "thirty-one lamps from the dawn" — Euclid confirms 31 ancient quasars (z 6.6–7.8, two the most ancient ever, first ~670 Myr; Yang et al., A&A, 6 Jul; a dark-energy survey as the best ancient-lamp hunter — rhymes with Vera Rubin No. 36; sharpens the early-SMBH-growth puzzle) + Hayabusa2's Torifune flyby (JAXA, 7 Jul, ~800m, a contact binary); in-brief = fossil-tooth-socket bee nurseries (Royal Society Open Science) + GWTC-5 (~390 GW detections; No. 23/25); 3I/ATLAS closed. LOVE & LIFE: "when she earns more, the old explanation fails" — a Journal of Marriage and Family study (via PsyPost 8 Jul) replicates the higher-earning-woman break-up pattern but finds the traditional-gender-norms explanation doesn't hold — the risk is the unrenegotiated household, not her income (re-mark the positions, don't blame the old marks); companions = a 3-type romantic-deception taxonomy (JSPR) + couples' "contagious forgetting"; observational caveats; not counselling advice. FITNESS: "the brake on ageing muscle — and the pedal that releases it" — Duke-NUS / Autophagy: with age DEAF1 rises → mTORC1 overdrive → autophagy suppressed → muscle repair stalls; exercise activates FOXO which lowers DEAF1 (the molecular "use it or lose it"; mouse/cell model — NOT a prescription; sobering nuance = in very old muscle exercise alone may not fully restore repair → the argument for starting at 45 not 60); UCLA NDRG1 (3 Jul) complements; the settled prescription (strength+cardio ~45% mortality, 90–120min sweet spot, Nos. 28/32/34) is UNCHANGED; "no DEAF1 pill" sceptic; general guidance, not medical advice. THE DIARY (2pp): SG — NDP 2026/SG61 (★ 9 Aug, first indoor 300-drone show, NE shows 11 & 18 Jul), F1 Exhibition Asian debut (★ 23 Jul–18 Oct Gardens by the Bay, tickets on sale S$29–49), Creators Super Fest (11–12 Jul), Legally Blonde musical (29 Jul), the Weeknd (2–3 Oct), Post Malone (22 Aug), 5SOS (10–11 Nov), BTS ARIRANG (★ 17/19/20/22 Dec) + a stadium-Q4 booking note; Japan — teamLab Borderless new exhibition (★ 8 Jul–8 Oct "On the Asymmetry of the Universe"), Gion Matsuri (★ 17 & 24 Jul), Sumida Fireworks (25 Jul), Fuji Rock (24–26 Jul), Aki Basho sumo (13–27 Sep, tickets on-sale 8 Aug), BIGBANG HK (13–15 Nov) + planning notes. STANDING CHASE: BIGBANG SG (17 Oct) on-sale STILL unannounced (5th issue chasing; "Coming Soon" via b.stage). THE TABLE (rotated, fresh, honesty rule): Mimmo Bakery Café (Asia Square CBD; HK Quarry Bay import, pistachio bolo bao/HK egg tart; the batch's VERIFIED HIT — SETHLUI/DFD/Eatbook unanimous, LEAD) + Casa Mori (Dempsey; Willin Low × José Alonso Spanish-mod-Sin, one warm review in, pedigree bet) + Hi Stranger (Neil Rd; shape-shifting "chapters" cocktail bar, too new to call) + Rolls (Club St temaki bar, details held); Blue Box Café status-check (No. 36 lead, STILL not open — "mid-July," too new to call, honoured); Cookhouse by Koufu (Changi T2 24/7 airside) note. Not relisted: FreakyNoods/Yi Man Fen/Madeleine's/Cookboys (No. 36); Hikiniku to Come stays RETIRED (No. 28); Bouillon Gavroche flagged as stale-recirculating. PHOTO EDITION heroes (4, all verified/representative from their Commons file pages, honestly labelled): Marina Bay at dusk — File:Singapore Marina Bay Dusk 2018-02-27.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song (representative, Singapore); chips on a wafer — File:Chips on 6-Inch-Wafer 01.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, Kuebi/Armin Kübelbeck (representative, Technology); personal audio — File:Headphones 1.jpg, CC BY-SA 2.5 (representative, NOT the Nothing Ear 3a, The Kit); the deep sky — File:ESO - Milky Way.jpg, CC BY 4.0, ESO (representative, Curiosities). The cover "declared vs built rings" hero, the World-Cup bracket, the Macro four-instrument strip/tables, the RAM-price bars, the sensor-comparison, the sideline-timeline, the cosmic-clock timeline and the essay's "two ways to end" figure kept as original SVG (no forced photo). THE LONG READ (3pp): "The Sense of an Ending" — the declared ending (a peace pronounced over; a market that un-priced it) vs the built ending (a rail loop finished on schedule after 17 yrs), via Frank Kermode's The Sense of an Ending (1967) ("tick-tock," "in the middest" — we impose endings reality doesn't offer), the Compiègne (1918/1940) & Panmunjom (1953) armistices (declarations mistaken for settlements; Fromkin's A Peace to End All Peace), Fukuyama's 1989 "end of history" (the ultimate tock), and the counter-image of Amiens Cathedral (patience organised into stone; the tree whose shade you'll never sit in, No. 36); the discipline = distrust endings that arrive as sentences, honour the ones that arrive as last pieces; "only the patient actually finish things"; Ecclesiastes anchor; callbacks to the harvest-lag (No. 36) & homecoming-as-practice (No. 35). Editorial theme: an ending is built, not declared.

issues.title: The Print
issues.quote: When you can measure what you are speaking about, and express it in numbers, you know something about it … but when you cannot measure it … your knowledge is of a meagre and unsatisfactory kind.

issues.spine: the high-water mark — a peak is confirmable only from its far side; mark the visible water, flag the unseen depth, call neither shoreline nor bottom permanent
issues.title: The High-Water Mark
issues.quote: I turn the wheel that spins; I delight to see the high come down and the low ascend.
issues.author: Boethius, The Consolation of Philosophy, Bk II (c. 524) — the voice of Fortune
issues.text: Weekday Edition (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp; news-forward; no Travel Desk; The Macro Desk standing). Issue spine: the high-water mark — a peak is confirmable only from its far side; mark the visible water, flag the unseen depth, call neither shoreline nor bottom permanent. Threads: gold −25% off the 28 Jan ATH, oil −40% off the war peak, the dollar at a 13-month high, the inflation gauge at an expected peak, the UK landslide curdled. THE WORLD (2pp, four viewpoints Washington/Tehran/Vienna-IAEA/Beijing): the LEAD — one signature, two road maps — the Islamabad Memorandum (signed remotely 17 Jun) is read two ways: Washington (Vance/Trump: inspectors back "this week") vs Tehran (Baghaei/Gharibabadi: "no clear schedule," only after a final deal); IAEA's Grossi broke silence Wed 24 Jun at Fukushima ("day after tomorrow or in 10 days"); last verified stockpile 13 Jun 2025 = 441 kg 60%-HEU; Hormuz reopening contested (~35–39 vessels Mon 22 Jun ≈ ⅓ of pre-war flow; IMO evacuating 11,000 seafarers; US 60-day waiver freed ~67M bbl, Chinese refiners the biggest buyers). SECONDARY — Starmer resigned (Mon 22 Jun; the 2024 174-seat landslide curdled in ~18 months) → Burnham (won Makerfield by-election 18 Jun ~54.8%, Streeting-backed, ~200 MPs; nominations 9–16 Jul; PM ~17–18 Jul; would be the 7th UK leader in a decade) + Lebanon truce frayed (2 killed Tue 24 Jun) + Colombia (de la Espriella 43.7% v Cepeda 40.9%) + Ukraine refinery strikes one-line. THE LONG READ (3pp): "The High-Water Mark" — a peak is named only from its far side — via the leadsman's "mark twain" (2 fathoms → Samuel Clemens's pen name), the Gettysburg "High Water Mark of the Rebellion" / Pickett's Charge (3 Jul 1863, named only in retrospect), Irving Fisher's "permanently high plateau" (16 Oct 1929, the top mis-called) and King Canute / Henry of Huntingdon (the humility reading — staged to prove he cannot command the tide); the landing = diversification means not needing to call the top if you are not all-in, and this week the blend held (equities took the AI stress-test, bonds rallied); callbacks Hegel (No. 29, owl/dusk), Lao Tzu (No. 22), Churchill (No. 30) & Boethius (this issue). issues.spine: the opening of the line — the difference between a ribbon-cutting and a thing that actually carries load; ride it / find the gold spike / read the print
issues.title: The Opening of the Line
issues.quote: We shape our buildings; thereafter they shape us.
issues.author: Winston Churchill (House of Commons, 28 Oct 1943)
issues.text: Weekday Edition (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp; news-forward; no Travel Desk; The Macro Desk standing). Issue spine: the opening of the line — the difference between a ribbon-cutting and a thing that actually carries load; ride it / find the gold spike / read the print. THE WORLD (2pp, four viewpoints Washington/Tehran/Beijing/London): the LEAD — after the cancelled Lucerne ceremony (No. 27), US & Iran signed a road map to a final deal within 60 days at the Bürgenstock resort (high-level committee + working groups on nuclear/sanctions/dispute-resolution; a Lebanon de-confliction cell), but the deal's first claim cracked within hours — Vance said Iran agreed to readmit IAEA inspectors & that US/Qatar would approve use of unfrozen assets; Tehran contradicted both ("current procedures" only; "Iran is the only country who decides"); Pezeshkian: "never back down from the right to enrich"; Brent 30M bbl/week, first Saudi cargoes, US 60-day oil licence); Pentagon seeks US$80bn for the war. SECONDARY — Starmer resigned (Mon 22 Jun; nominations 9–16 Jul, new PM by 1 Sep if contested; 7th UK leader in a decade) + Lebanon truce frayed (2 killed Tue) + Colombia confirmed (de la Espriella 43.7% v Cepeda 40.9%) + Ukraine refinery strikes one-line. SINGAPORE: the LEAD — the East Coast joins the network: Thomson–East Coast Line Stage 4 (Tanjong Rhu–Bayshore) opened to passengers 23 Jun (free preview 21 Jun) — the East Coast's first MRT spine, the edition's spine in concrete (a line that bears load day one), clean hand-off to Property/Bayshore; + retirement age 63→64 / re-employment 68→69 from 1 Jul; May CPI delta (Apr 1.8%/1.4% core; core ~2.5% by Aug per RHB/UOB); NODX +38.4% one-line; nuclear/SMR parked at 2027 (Asia Nuclear & SMR summit SG 30 Jun–1 Jul); STI record ~5,217. PROPERTY (pivoted off rates, saturated): the LEAD — the price lands on 15 July: with Bayshore newly on the rail map, the Bayshore Drive mixed-use GLS (tender noon 15 Jul, ~S$1,150–1,250 psf ppr est.; first parcel SingHaiyi–Garnet S$1,388 Mar) becomes the East-Coast benchmark a paused market awaits (developer sales 447 in May, 3-mo low; URA Q1 +0.9% final; HDB resale −0.1%); construction-cost floor (>S$2,400 psf break-even) as structural support; Sembawang Drive EC (first test of the 8 May overhaul, No. 28) + 2H GLS + SORA "still on the shelf." TECHNOLOGY (2pp): the LEAD (Silicon & Sovereignty) — frontier-class AI boards at consumer prices: AMD Ryzen AI "Halo"/Strix Halo dev platform at Micro Center (pre-orders Jun; 128GB unified, 70B-class local inference at ~half the DGX Spark price) as the consumer answer to the memory tax (No. 24), set against the circular-financing scrutiny that drove Monday's 22 Jun tech sell-off (Nvidia↔OpenAI ~$100bn loop — "capital that circulates vs capital that carries"); H200/China one-line. p8 (The Home Lab): the build — Gemma 4 12B (3 Jun, fits 16GB, encoder-free multimodal) + Ollama 0.30 (Jun GGUF/MLX) + LM Studio MLX KV-cache (No. 29) into Home Assistant; the 24GB sweet spot (Qwen 3.6 4-bit); "16GB is the new floor"; open-weight frontier "still on the shelf." THE KIT: the LEAD — Audio-Technica ATH-WP900SE × Fujigen (closed-back wired; earcups in Fujigen's guitar maple + 3-tone sunburst lacquer, first time on a headphone) as the craft object "indifferent to the AI-hardware cycle"; secondary Microsoft Surface Pro (Qualcomm X2, ~53% graphics) + a Fluance turntable; "still on the shelf" (Sony 1000X ColleXion, Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max, Snap Specs, Meze Arta, WiiM Bar, Xreal R1). CONNECTED HOME: the LEAD — "now you can see your own mesh": Home Assistant's 23 Jun rebuild of its Matter engine onto matter.js (open-source TS), upgrade to Matter 1.5.1, a new Thread mesh visualisation + OTBR Thread 1.4 — the local-first reliability upgrade ("see the hops you own"); Matter 1.6/Joint Fabric one-line (No. 26, announced ≠ adopted); HA 2026.6 continuity. THE GOOD LIFE: the LEAD — the soft-yen Japan window (USD/JPY ~¥161.5, near 1980s lows; SGD/JPY ~¥126; early-July connoisseur window; tax-free reform 1 Nov) + an honest-caveat box (a soft yen is the visitor's gift & the host's strain); the OBJECT (rotated to an independent) = Atelier Wen Perception V3 "Yún" (13 Jun; hand-guilloché, the thing made better by iteration) — watches/audio saturation avoided; GS-in-Ginza one-line. SCREEN & SOUND: the LEAD — Supergirl's opening is the verdict (Milly Alcock / Jason Momoa; intl rollout from 24 Jun, US open Fri 26 Jun; tracking collapsed to ~US$40–51M on a ~US$175M budget; first reactions split; "judge the gate, not the guess" — held honestly, no pre-judged number); secondary Charli XCX Music, Fashion, Film announced (24 Jul); Strokes Reality Awaits / Muse The Wow! Signal both 26 Jun one-line (No. 28); Olivia Rodrigo CLOSED/saturated. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): the LEAD — protect the sleep (the June SG school-holiday window as a body-clock reset): a University of Oregon weekend-recovery-sleep/anxiety finding + AAP/AASM 9–12h & regular sleep-wake timing as the load-bearing foundation; a "try this week" box (anchor wake-time ±1h, morning daylight, screens out of the bedroom) + a "don't be alarmist" box (a livable average, not a compliance regime) + the evidence page (parent's own use #1 predictor No. 28; relationships the buffer No. 25–26; affluent-home criticism risk No. 29); deliberately NOT screen-time (saturated); general guidance, not medical advice. THE MACRO DESK ("The Big Picture", standing): the chain — FOMC hawkish HOLD 3.50–3.75% (17 Jun, Warsh; No. 27–29 delta) + inflation near a 3-yr high → US 10Y ~4.46% / dollar bid (DXY ~1-yr high) → war premium draining from Brent (~US$77, 3-mo low) & gold (~US$4,140, −25% from the 28 Jan peak) as Hormuz reopens → USD/JPY ~¥161.5 (explains the Good Life soft yen) → May PCE due Thu 25 Jun = "awaiting the print" (the spine in a data release); regime = higher-for-longer / dollar-bid / risk-capped (No. 28 delta); standing close = positive equity–bond correlation, diversification doing less for VWRA & global bonds; VWRA/AGGU held qualitatively (no fabricated prints); education-not-advice. CURIOSITIES: the LEAD — a door to the Moon's depths: the South Pole–Aitken impact excavated deep-mantle material near the Artemis III landing sites (astronauts may walk on rock from hundreds of km down; ScienceDaily 22 Jun) — "a line to the deep interior opened by an ancient collision"; secondaries = black-hole winds quenching giant galaxies + an early flickering quasar (~850 Myr post-Big-Bang); "neutrino factory" galaxy one-line (No. 28). LOVE & LIFE: the LEAD — the receding marital horizon (IFS State of Our Unions 2026: marriage still expected by most yet only ~1-in-3 actively dating, the wedding always a few years out — "a blueprint everyone keeps and no one breaks ground on") with a warm mid-40s turn (the long-built relationship is the load-bearing line); self-report/US-sample caveat; No. 19/20 callbacks. FITNESS ("The Long Game"): the LEAD — measure the structure, don't track the score: demonstrable strength (grip, chair-stand) predicts survival largely independent of aerobic activity (LaMonte et al., JAMA Network Open 2026 — older-women cohort, magnitudes don't transfer) + a no-wearable quarterly field-test (dead-hang / sit-to-stand / timed stairs); sceptic box (observational; grip as marker as much as cause); strength-volume sweet-spot (No. 18) SATURATED callback only; general guidance, not medical advice. THE DIARY (2pp): the marquee ★ = BIGBANG 20/26 World Tour, National Stadium Sat 17 Oct 2026 — the gates begin to open (VIP presale 24 Jun; global GA on-sale Fri 26 Jun 10am local for the US/Europe dates); the SG on-sale date/price STILL pending (register b.stage; the "11 Sep" figure is the New Jersey date, not SG) — honesty box; SG (Dragon Boat 27–28 Jun, GastroBeats/World Cup screenings, DRUM TAO→12 Jul, Children's Festival, NDP 9 Aug, F1+EXO/Mitski autumn) + Japan soft-yen (Mt Fuji opens 1 Jul, Tanabata 7 Jul, Gion 17 & 24 Jul, Tenjin 24–25 Jul, Fuji Rock 24–26 Jul, Sumida late Jul, Nagoya Sumo) + a "planning notes" box (the crowded October: F1 + BIGBANG collide) + a "Plan the flights" box; region (Naadam 11–13 Jul, Rainforest WMF Sarawak, Boryeong Mud). THE TABLE (rotated, fresh, honesty rule): Carlitos Casa de Comidas (Spanish, Joo Chiat, suckling pig — the lead, "too new to call") + Visitors Cafe (Korean-style brunch, Tanjong Pagar Plaza — viral) + NiKU iKU (halal Japanese grill dine-in, Tampines Hub/Lot One — the value/halal pick) + Freshio Gelato (2nd outlet, KADA Maxwell — a real new peg); prior venues (Asin, Obongzip, Between Buns, Torikizoku, etc.) not re-listed. PHOTO EDITION heroes (6, all verified from their Commons file pages, honestly labelled): Strait of Hormuz — File:Strait of Hormuz (MODIS 2020-12-04).jpg, PD-NASA/MODIS (representative, leads The World); Marina Bay at dusk — File:Singapore Marina Bay Dusk 2018-02-27.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song (representative, Singapore); Servers in a Rack — File:Servers in a Rack.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, Abigor (representative, Technology); Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi — File:Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi (2015-10-26).jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Alpsdake (representative, The Good Life/Japan); Full Moon — File:FullMoon2010.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, Gregory H. Revera (representative, Curiosities); the Golden Spike ceremony — File:East and West Shaking hands at the laying of last rail Union Pacific Railroad.jpg, PD, Andrew J. Russell 1869 (actual subject, leads The Long Read). The cover "opening line"/route hero, the circulates-vs-carries diagram, the Thread-mesh figure, the SPA-basin schematic, the Macro market tables, the "ribbon or load" threads figure and all conceptual/data figures kept as original SVG (no forced photo). THE LONG READ (3pp): "The Opening of the Line" — Churchill's "we shape our buildings; thereafter they shape us" drawn through the week's openings, anchored to the Metropolitan Railway / first London Underground (10 Jan 1863, the doubted blueprint that bore ~38,000 passengers on day one), the Golden Spike at Promontory Summit (10 May 1869 — the soft gold spike tapped in then pulled out & replaced with iron: "the ceremony used a spike that could not hold a train") and the Tōkaidō Shinkansen (1 Oct 1964, nine days before the Tokyo Olympics — the "outdated" bet that re-made Japan); counter-case = ribbons that never bore load (Kellogg–Briand No. 13, Versailles No. 23); the field-guide = ride it / find the gold spike / what will it shape; callbacks Hegel (No. 29, the verdict comes later), Milton (No. 23, arrival is a beginning), Lao Tzu (No. 22, the useful emptiness — a railway is mostly tunnel). Editorial theme: the opening of the line / ribbon vs load.

issues.spine: the verdict comes later
issues.title: The Owl of Minerva
issues.quote: The owl of Minerva spreads its wings only with the falling of the dusk.
issues.author: G.W.F. Hegel, Elements of the Philosophy of Right, Preface (1820)
issues.text: Weekday Edition (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp; news-forward; no Travel Desk; The Macro Desk standing). issues.title: Taken at the Flood

issues.spine: the changing of the guard — when a guard changes, ask whether the OFFICE is changing or only the OFFICER
issues.title: The Changing of the Guard
issues.quote: The old order changeth, yielding place to new, / And God fulfils himself in many ways, / Lest one good custom should corrupt the world.
issues.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson, Idylls of the King, "The Passing of Arthur" (1869)
issues.text: Weekday Edition (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp; news-forward balance). Issue spine: the changing of the guard — when a guard changes, ask whether the OFFICE is changing or only the OFFICER. Five handovers thread the book: the chair (Powell→Warsh), the war (combat→reconstruction), the grid (gas→nuclear), the standard (proprietary→Matter), the franchise (toy→screen). THE WORLD (2pp, "The deal · the gathering · the comedown"): the LEAD — the US–Iran peace is "now complete" (announced 14 Jun by Pakistan PM Sharif + Trump; electronic signature, formal ceremony Switzerland Fri 19 Jun; Hormuz reopens toll-free / blockade lifted but mines remain → opens "for mine removal" only after signing; war began 28 Feb 2026) set beside the 52nd G7 summit at Évian-les-Bains (15–17 Jun, Macron host, Altman invited, Zelenskyy Tue session no bilateral, transatlantic grievances) — "the document arrives Friday; the working strait takes longer"; the read-through = FOMC 16–17 Jun is Warsh's first meeting (sworn 22 May after a 54-45 vote), hold at 3.50–3.75% near-certain, watch the dot-plot + Warsh's Wed presser; Brent ~US$83 (2-mo low, −>4% on the deal, still ~+20% vs the ~US$70 pre-war floor, late-Mar peak ~US$113); secondaries = World Bank's 2.5% 2026 growth cut, Colombia's 21 Jun runoff. SINGAPORE: the LEAD — "the energy succession stops being hypothetical": after the worst shock since 1973, SG's long civil-nuclear pivot (US/Japan/Korea cooperation frameworks; EMA–KHNP SMR MOU 2 Mar; Mott MacDonald feasibility study; nuclear moved from "distant possibility" to "named option") with Asia Nuclear Energy & SMR 2026 hosted in SG 30 Jun–1 Jul as the peg; Q2 tariff 29.72¢/kWh, July step-up on lagged gas; relief calendar (June CDC→Jul U-Save→Aug GSTV→Sep COL); Q1 GDP 6%, Apr CPI 1.8%; WP/Pritam a one-line delta (saturated). PROPERTY: "the floor under prices is poured, not rented" — a peace dividend won't reach the build cost; URA Q1 +0.9% final (slowest 8 qtrs), OCR +1.3%, landed −1.8%, HDB resale −0.1%; 35% foreign ABSD; ~8,500 launches 2026 (+40% y/y); new EC rules (8 May: 10-yr MOP / 15-yr privatisation); Peck Hay GLS to CDL/Hong Leong S$542.4m; the construction-cost floor (>S$2,400 psf GLS break-even) as the structural support; SORA & June BTO one-line "still on the shelf." TECHNOLOGY (2pp): the LEAD — the other AI bill, memory: Microsoft's 2026 capex swells to ~US$190bn, ~US$25bn of it attributable to the DRAM/HBM price surge (32GB DDR5 ~US$95→~US$575; "the memory tax") — the chip is the easy part, the RAM is the moat; Home Lab page = buy the verified box now, memory is the binding constraint; Nvidia Vera CPUs in full production (Anthropic/OpenAI/SpaceX) + RTX/DGX Spark continuity; open-weight frontier (GLM-5.1/Kimi K2.6/DeepSeek V4-Pro) "still on the shelf"; WWDC Gemini-Siri & H200 delta-only. THE KIT: the LEAD — Razer Project Motoko (AI cameras embedded in headphone ear-cups, model-agnostic, dev kit Q2) read through a "walls you wear" privacy-sceptic lens — the portable cousin of the listening home; "still on the shelf" strip (LG C6 OLED, Insta360 Mic Pro, Garmin FR70/170, Fitbit Air, a7R VI, Momentum 5). CONNECTED HOME: "a universal remote — but whose box?" — CSA "Unify" Austin 16–18 Jun (this week) + Matter 1.5 cameras shipping (SmartThings/Aqara/Eve) + IKEA's 20+ Thread-native push; "standardises the buttons, not the back end"; a migrator's shortlist (local NAS recording / Thread / works-with-HA); HA 2026.6 + homeOS/HomePad continuity one-liners. THE GOOD LIFE: "the window stays open — even as Tokyo moves" — BoJ meets 16–17 Jun, a hike to 1% likely (first since Dec 2025) yet the yen sits ~¥159, so the early-July soft-yen window holds; the succession motif reaches Tokyo too — Gov. Ueda hospitalised, Dep. Gov. Himino chairs (the stand-in, mirror of Warsh); the OBJECT = the Patek Cubitus (the divisive Nautilus-heir, US$45.5k steel → US$187.5k skeleton, ~2× secondary) as a literal changing of the guard, with Grand Seiko's Ushio Diver (9RB1, US$12,400) the soft-yen counterpoint; auctions CLOSED (Nos. 22–23 callback). SCREEN & SOUND: the LEAD — Toy Story 5's review embargo lifts today (16 Jun) — a franchise that has never scored below 96% returns (predicted ~92–93% RT) with a premise about technology stealing a child's attention (Andrew Stanton dir.; Hanks/Allen/Cusack; a Taylor Swift end-credits song; opens US 19 Jun) — a fifth act that is itself a baton-pass; Olivia Rodrigo a closed callback; Spielberg's Disclosure Day / Avatar-to-Disney+ continuity. THE FAMILY DESK (2pp): the LEAD — Common Sense Media's first annual census "AI Use by Tweens and Teens (2026)" (AI as confidant — unsafe under 18; ~¾ say school set rules but only ~half were taught safe use; ~half never discussed AI safety with a parent) arriving the same week as the Toy Story premise & ambient Gemini-Siri, with a shared-space / name-what-it-is / monitoring-and-modelling toolkit + an evidence page (Nagata/UCSF) + a "don't be alarmist" box (2023 Oxford near-zero link); general guidance, not medical advice. THE DIARY (2pp): SG — Dragon Boat (★ 19 Jun, races 27–28), i Light (to 28 Jun), GastroBeats (to 28 Jun), Takashimaya Food Fiesta, Snoopy@Changi (to 12 Jul), DRUM TAO (25 Jun–12 Jul), NDP (★ 9 Aug); Japan (soft yen ~¥159) — Mt Fuji opens (★ 1 Jul), Nagoya Sumo (12–26 Jul), Gion (★ 17 & 24 Jul), Tenjin (24–25 Jul), Sumida fireworks (★ 25 Jul). THE TABLE (rotated, fresh): Satori (Amoy St charcoal yakitori counter, skewers from S$3.80, NOT halal — LEAD, "too new to call"), Centro (Shaw Lido cinema-dining, Australian all-day) + a "now reviewed" callback Jiin Omakase (Les Amis, Shaw Centre, opened 8 May — verdict in, warm; lunch S$138++/dinner S$288++) + a notable-change peg Dumpling Darlings 3rd outlet (New Bahru flagship). PHOTO EDITION heroes (5, all verified from their Commons file pages, honestly labelled representative): Strait of Hormuz — File:Strait of Hormuz (MODIS 2020-12-04).jpg, PD-NASA (representative 2020 satellite view, leads The World); Marina Bay at dusk — File:Singapore Marina Bay Dusk 2018-02-27.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song (Singapore); a server rack — File:Servers in a Rack.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0, Abigor (representative, leads Technology); JWST deep field — File:Webb's First Deep Field.jpg, PD (NASA/ESA/CSA) (representative SMACS 0723, NOT the "little red dots" data, leads Curiosities); Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi — File:Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi s2.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Alpsdake (the Diary/Japan); the cover baton-over-globe hero, the Brent sparkline, the Fed-chairs "one rail, many hands" relay figure, the memory-tax price-ramp & all conceptual figures kept as original SVG; remaining desks kept Meridian artwork (no forced photo). THE LONG READ: "The Changing of the Guard" — an office outlives its holder; what transfers is the mandate and the unfinished work, not the person — via the medieval "le roi est mort, vive le roi" / le mort saisit le vif (Charles VII, 1422) and Kantorowicz's The King's Two Bodies (1957, the body natural vs the body politic), the Roman five-day interrex holding the auspices in trust (the modern stand-in — Himino for Ueda), and central-bank succession as the deliberately-boring transfer (Volcker→…→Powell→Warsh); the test = sort each handover into cosmetic (office built to outlive the officer → keep your nerve) vs structural (the work is unfinished & must be operated → pay attention); callbacks to Heraclitus (No. 19), Seneca (No. 20), Lao Tzu (No. 22) & Milton (No. 23). Editorial theme: the changing of the guard / office vs officer.

issues.spine: the thing that finally arrived — arrival is a beginning, not an end; the victories of peace are the day-after work
issues.title: Peace Hath Her Victories
issues.quote: Peace hath her victories, no less renown'd than war.
issues.author: John Milton, Sonnet XVI, "To the Lord General Cromwell" (1652)
issues.text: Weekday Edition (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp; returns to news-forward balance after the No. 21/22 weekend pair). Issue spine: the thing that finally arrived — arrival is a beginning, not an end; the victories of peace are the day-after work. THE WORLD (2pp, four viewpoints Tehran/Washington/Beijing/Vienna-IAEA): the LEAD — after 22 editions "described in every capital, signed in none," a US–Iran peace DEAL IS REACHED (announced Sun 14 Jun by Pakistan PM Sharif; signing ceremony set Fri 19 Jun, Switzerland; Hormuz to reopen "toll-free," blockade lifted, frozen Iranian assets released, a reconstruction clause written in), with the day-after caveat front-loaded (Morgan Stanley: mine-clearing, restarting idled fields & re-pricing insurance take months — "a deal you can't yet ship"); oil eased (~US$86 Brent, still ~+23% vs the ~US$70 pre-war floor); secondaries = World Bank's 2026 global-growth cut to 2.5%, Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% v Cepeda 40.9%), Ukraine's Volgograd-refinery drone strike. SINGAPORE: "Relief built for a war that may be ending" — 95% of power from imported gas; Q2 tariff 29.72¢/kWh set on Jan–mid-Mar gas so the July step-up still bites on a lag even as peace arrives; the pre-positioned relief calendar (June CDC vouchers → Jul U-Save → Aug GSTV → Sep COL); Q1 GDP 6%, Apr CPI 1.8%; Oct SAF flight levy S$3–16; WP/Pritam 28 Jun a one-line delta (saturated). PROPERTY: "Fewer launches, firmer floor" — 17 launches/~8,100 units 2026 (−30% y/y); URA Q1 +0.9% final (slowest in 8 qtrs); ABSD (Dec 2025) still biting; the construction-cost floor (build +40%/decade, GLS break-evens >S$2,400 psf) as the structural support under prices; Lentor Central final GLS parcel peg; 2H GLS ~4,745 units; HDB resale −0.1% & June BTO/SORA kept to one-line "still on the shelf." TECHNOLOGY (2pp): the LEAD — "the peace won't pay the power bill": US data-centre demand modelled ~80→150 GW by 2028, DOE's "Agora" grid simulator (2 Jun), 300+ state bills, Carnegie Mellon ~8% household-bill rise by 2030 (25%+ Virginia); Nvidia's Vera CPU enters full production (OpenAI/Anthropic/SpaceX named) + RTX Spark continuity (No. 18); Home Lab page = tokens-per-watt & the sovereign/own-it angle (desk-class boxes ~250W); open-weight frontier (GLM-5.1/Kimi K2.6/DeepSeek V4-Pro) "still on the shelf"; WWDC Gemini-Siri & H200 delta-only. THE KIT: the LEAD — "who owns the band on your wrist": Whoop wins a US injunction blocking a rival (Lexqi) read through the subscription-moat lens for an Oura+Whoop owner; Meta smartwatch reported for this year; a war-premium-fades buying note; own-vs-subscribe contrarian; "still on the shelf" strip (Garmin FR70/170, Fitbit Air, a7R VI, Momentum 5, Canon gimbal, smart glasses). issues.spine: the imagined and the real — fear & imagination running ahead of reality

THE WORLD (2pp, four viewpoints Tehran/Washington/Beijing/Islamabad): the LEAD — oil whipsaws on a single Trump post (threat to seize Kharg Island & take "total control" of Iran's oil → Brent toward US$93, then −4% on "sign a deal soon," settle US$90.38, −3% d/d, ~+30% vs the ~US$70 pre-war) on Day 3 of renewed US–Iran strikes; the one piece of HARD damage = the World Bank cutting 2026 global growth to 2.5% (from 2.9%, weakest since the pandemic; downside 1.3%; infl ~4%; euro 0.8%, China 4.2%, India 6.6%; US$60bn liquidity) + the ECB's first major war-driven hike (+25bp) & a hot US PPI, Fed decides next week; Hormuz MOU one-line delta; secondaries = Colombia 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% v Cepeda 40.9%), Ukraine refinery strikes (Volgograd offline). issues.spine: the price of fire — energy as the master input re-pricing everything

issues.spine: the rented mind — the outsourced faculty

issues.quote: Insist on yourself; never imitate.

issues.text: Weekday Edition (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp). Issue spine: the rented mind — the outsourced faculty. THE WORLD (2pp, side-by-side viewpoints): the LEAD — Israel & Iran traded direct missile strikes (8 Jun, first since the 8 Apr ceasefire) over Israel's Lebanon offensive; Iran said operations "ended," Netanyahu halted "for now" but "not over"; Brent spiked ~5% intraday past US$98 then settled US$94.25 (WTI US$91.30), +31% vs the eve of conflict 100 days ago; OPEC+ +188k b/d July, China imports a 10-yr low cushioning, JPM base ~US$100 rest-2026 vs Fitch ~US$70 from Sept; the Hormuz 60-day MOU still "described in every capital, signed in none," Polymarket signing-by-15-Jun odds in single digits; viewpoints Tehran / Washington / Beijing / Islamabad (mediator); secondaries = Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%, Valencia's endorsement, running-mate split) & Ukraine's long-range refinery strikes (Volgograd offline). SINGAPORE: the WP's 28 Jun secret-ballot cadres conference over Pritam Singh — DELTA = PPP's Goh Meng Seng open letter urging removal ("convicted liar") drawing pushback, CEC's "judgement calls" framing, Law Society → Court of Three Judges; the relief calendar (June CDC vouchers, Jul U-Save/S&CC, Aug GSTV, Sept COL) vs the energy squeeze (Jul tariff 29.72c/kWh); Q1 GDP 6%, Apr CPI 1.8%, STI 4,963. PROPERTY (pivoted off rates per editor — reader flagged rate-coverage fatigue): the LEAD — the Prime-heavy June 2026 BTO (~6,900 flats, 7 projects across Ang Mo Kio / Bishan / Bukit Merah / Sembawang / Woodlands; ~47% Prime, ~5% Plus, ~48% Standard) & the historic Lakeview/Shunfu return (~1,200 units by Marymount MRT/MacRitchie, first new HDB there in 40+ years) — owner read-through = Prime's 10-yr MOP, subsidy clawback & resale income-ceiling deliberately thin the future resale pool; SECONDARY = URA's 2H2026 GLS Confirmed List (announced 3 Jun — nine sites, ~4,745 private units incl. 735 EC; pipeline ~57k→~61k as a "supply tap stays open" signal); HDB RPI 203.4 −0.1% Q1 (continuity); the SORA/refinancing-window story GRACEFULLY DEMOTED to a single line. TECHNOLOGY (2pp): the LEAD — WWDC 2026 (Cook's likely-last keynote → Ternus CEO 1 Sept) rebuilds Siri on a custom ~1.2T-param Google Gemini run on Google Cloud (~US$1B/yr), a three-tier "Foundation Models" stack (on-device AFM → AFM Cloud → AFM Cloud Pro/Gemini), not in the EU/China at launch, macOS 27 ends Intel, iPhone 11 kept on iOS 27, a US$250M Siri-delay settlement — framed as "rent the model, own the routing, manufacture the devices"; the home lab — the memory tax as the binding constraint (32GB DDR5 ~US$95 mid-2025 → ~US$550–600 peak, DDR5 chip $6.84 Sep → $27.20 Dec, HBM ~3:1 wafer ratio, rally projected past 2028); open-weight frontier "still on the shelf," H200 delta only.
