PHOTO EDITION heroes (verified from Commons pages): a crude-oil tanker (CC BY-SA 4.0, Steven Pavlov — representative, leads The World); Singapore Marina Bay dusk (CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song — Singapore); HDB flats, Kallang (CC BY-SA 4.0 — representative, leads Property); Mt Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi (CC BY 3.0, Midori — representative spring image, leads the Diary's Japan page); cover wireframe-globe, the oil sparkline, the SORA-crossover, the three-tier-routing diagram, the DDR5 price-ramp, the protoplanet schematic & the Long Read's "threads" figure all kept as original SVG. THE LONG READ: "The Rented Mind" — the outsourced faculty (self-reliance vs borrowed power) across Apple renting Gemini, the listening home, AI companions, the pill vs the barbell & a mediated peace, via Plato's Phaedrus (Theuth & Thamus, writing as outsourced memory producing "the conceit of wisdom"), the Ottoman Janissaries & the Mamluks of Egypt (hired power that captured the state it served, abolition 1826) & Rome's Germanic foederati (outsourced frontier defence → Odoacer deposes the last Western emperor, 476) — with the test that the reversible dependence is leverage and the irreversible one a transfer of sovereignty; callbacks to Cicero (No. 16), Pasteur (No. 14) & Thoreau (No. 10); a closing "the threads · reversible or not" scorecard. Editorial theme: the rented mind / the outsourced faculty.

issues.spine: the memory supercycle — memory as the contested treasury
issues.title: The Treasury
issues.quote: Memory is the treasury and guardian of all things.
issues.author: Cicero, De Oratore (55 BC)
issues.text: First true Weekday Edition since the Sunday No. 15 (full twelve-desk weekday book, 24pp). Issue spine: the memory supercycle — memory as the contested treasury. THE WORLD (2pp, side-by-side viewpoints): the US–Iran framework still "described in every capital, signed in none" — Hezbollah's rejection of the US Lebanon ceasefire named as the obstacle, Iran warning US bases are "no longer safe," Polymarket's signed-by-15-Jun odds collapsing ~60%→~6%; Brent ~US$93 (−4.5% m/m, backwardated, China imports a 10-yr low, 6th straight inventory draw, an Oman Mina al-Fahal blast); secondaries = Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%, Valencia's endorsement) & Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian refineries (Volgograd offline). SINGAPORE: the WP's 28 Jun secret-ballot cadres conference over Pritam Singh — DELTA = Yee Jenn Jong's public "my vote is not secret, I'll back Pritam" at his book launch (3 Jun) + the Law Society's disciplinary referral to the Court of Three Judges; the relief calendar (S$500 CDC vouchers June, July U-Save/S&CC, Aug GSTV, Sept COL) tied to the energy squeeze (Siow); Q1 GDP 6%, Apr CPI 1.8%. PROPERTY: the 3M-SORA trough (~1.08%, modelled to bottom ~1% then ~1.39% by year-end; floating ~1.26% all-in / fixed ~1.35%, both $2M record) — vintage/provenance booming vs the modern-boutique slump (>40% of buyers under 40); Hermès quota logic + the soft yen. SCREEN & SOUND: the Carol Shields Prize 2026 to Julia Elliott's Hellions (short stories, 2 Jun Toronto, US$150k + Fogo Island) as the LEAD; Toy Story 5 (19 Jun firm), Nolan's Odyssey (demoted), Olivia Rodrigo's 3rd album (12 Jun), the Booker dozen (28 Jul). FAMILY (2pp): the AI-in-the-house LEAD (JAMA Network Open 2026 — ~20% of pre-teens, 9% of 8–9s use AI chatbots; Common Sense "no under-18 AI companions"; a red-team of 10 bots → unsafe advice) tied to Gemini-Siri arriving tonight, with shared-space / no-bedroom-overnight / AI-literacy guidance, a regulatory map (US KIDS Act, UK Online Safety Act, COPPA 2.0) & a "don't be alarmist" box. WHISPER: engagement/split season (Kravitz–Styles, Cabello–Chalhoub, Rapinoe–Bird, Halle Berry — all flagged). CURIOSITIES: JWST's diurnal MINERAL clouds on a hot giant ~700 ly off (clouds by dawn, clear by dusk) as the LEAD + the Venus–Jupiter conjunction tonight (8–9 Jun, closest until 2028) as a free naked-eye callback. LOVE & LIFE: romantic nostalgia as a couple's shared treasury (Evans/Wildschut/Sedikides 2022) — more commitment/closeness, with an honest "emotional-homeostasis / short-term dip" caveat. FITNESS: mitophagy as the LEAD — Urolithin A / Mitopure (a 2026 calcium-dependent-mitophagy study; RCTs ~12% strength, endurance, lower inflammation; >60% can't make UA from diet) with an honest sceptic box (modest effects, behind the free basics). DIARY (2pp): Venus–Jupiter (★) + Dragon Boat (27–28 Jun), HONNE (4–6 Aug), NDP (★ 9 Aug), Night Festival (late Aug); Japan — Mt Fuji opens ~1 Jul (Kawaguchiko fireworks 4 Jul), Nagoya Sumo (12–26 Jul), Sumida fireworks (★ 25 Jul), Gion/Tenjin; teamLab Planets art; BTS a Dec callback. THE TABLE (NEW): ASIN (Ace Tan, progressive Asian, 8-course $188++, opened 6 May — "too new to call"), Jiin Omakase (Les Amis, 8 May), Torikizoku (600-outlet Tokyo yakitori import, not halal), Obongzip (K-BBQ, 2nd outlet @ Star Vista) + "now reviewed" callbacks (Hikiniku to Come hype "warranted"; Bouillon Gavroche now open). PHOTO EDITION heroes (verified from Commons pages): Singapore Marina Bay (CC BY-SA 4.0, Benh Lieu Song); a crude-oil tanker (CC BY-SA 4.0, Steven Pavlov — representative, leads The World); HDB flats, Kallang (CC BY-SA 4.0, Martinpasquier — representative, leads Property); Mt Fuji over Lake Kawaguchi (CC BY 3.0, Midori — leads the Diary); cover memory-grid, the day/night cloud diagram & the Long Read's wafer-reallocation figure kept as original SVG. THE LONG READ: "The Treasury" — when a foundational substrate goes scarce it flows to its highest-margin use, and the durable fix is new capacity or substitution, not rationing, via Simonides of Ceos & Cicero's art of memory / the memory palace (De Oratore, 55 BC), the War Production Board's Feb-1942 civilian-auto ban (steel & rubber reallocated by decree) & the Haber-Bosch process (1909–13, scarcity abolished by pulling nitrogen from the air); callbacks to Pasteur (No. 14, reserves) & Thoreau (No. 10, the cost of a thing). Editorial theme: the memory supercycle / memory as the contested treasury.

issues.spine: the eve / reach exceeds grasp
issues.title: The Eve of Arrival
issues.quote: Ah, but a man's reach should exceed his grasp, / Or what's a heaven for?
issues.author: Robert Browning, Andrea del Sarto (1855)
issues.text: The Weekend Edition — first Sunday lifestyle-mode issue; continuity-correct vs No. 14. 24pp geared lifestyle: cover teasers led from Curiosities / Good Life / Kit, hard-news desks run lean. THE WORLD (2pp, TWO viewpoint panels): the Hormuz framework still "described in every capital, signed in none" — stalled over Lebanon, US escort suspended, Polymarket signing odds ~72%→~6%, Brent ~$93 — plus a reflective "slow news of a summer Sunday" digest (Colombia 21 Jun run-off; Ukraine St Petersburg/Volgograd strikes). SINGAPORE: the $500 CDC vouchers pulled forward to June (~S$1bn drawer plan, Siow) read as a household relief calendar; Q1 GDP 6%, Apr CPI 1.8%. PROPERTY: the 3M-SORA trough (~1.08%→~1.39% year-end) as a weekend refinancing job; HDB RPI −0.1% Q1. TECH: WWDC eve (8 Jun; Gemini-Siri, "27" betas, rumoured HomePad, Cook's likely-last keynote → Ternus Sept) + the home lab as a weekend project (open-weight field unchanged → "still on the shelf"; H200 one-line delta). KIT: Sony Xperia 1 VIII (NEW — jack/microSD/shutter, 48MP×3, ~S$1,989) + a "still on the shelf" strip (Oura 5 / a7R VI / Momentum 5 / smart-glasses; screwdriver-battery detail retired). CONNECTED HOME: a lifestyle "house that knows it's Sunday" feature (slow-morning scene, circadian lighting, local-first HA) — Matter 1.5 cameras CORRECTLY demoted to a one-line callback (No. 14), not re-led. GOOD LIFE: travel (Japan on a soft yen) + watch CULTURE ( 40% of Sotheby's buyers under 40; cooling top-end as connoisseurship) — the NY watch week demoted to a one-line "read the results, not the previews." SCREEN SOUND: a weekend "what to stream" (The Bear, House of the Dragon, the Lopez/Goldstein Netflix rom-com) + Rodrigo ADVANCED via a NEW angle (her Robert Smith duet revealed at Primavera Sound) + a one-line Women's Prize calendar note. FAMILY (2pp): a warm "screen-free Sunday" (SG June holidays; sleep/play/curiosity over controls; age-gates demoted to a one-liner) + a "don't be alarmist" evidence page. WHISPER: the Swift–Kelce summer-wedding rumour + engagement/split round-up (all flagged). CURIOSITIES: the Venus–Jupiter conjunction (8–9 Jun, ~1.6°, closest until 2028) as a free weekend assignment + the JWST cosmic-web map (5 Jun). LOVE LIFE: anticipation/savoring (the pre-event peak). FITNESS: the exercise + rapamycin/lamivudine trial a creatine RCT (Salem et al.) as longevity-lifestyle + the VO₂max-as-proxy sceptic. DIARY (centrepiece, 2pp): the conjunction as a free marquee + i Light / Children's Season + a NEW "where to eat this weekend" block (Tokyo cult imports Hikiniku to Come @ VivoCity Mensho X @ Raffles Pl; Bouillon Gavroche; Paul Pairet's Good Brunch) + the Tokyo summer-matsuri window (soft yen) + art; BTS demoted to a "now booking" callback (confirmed 17/19/20/22 Dec, tickets from 3 Jun). PHOTO EDITION heroes (verified from Commons pages): Singapore Marina Bay (CC BY-SA 4.0, blieusong); Strait of Hormuz USCGC (PD, USCG — representative); Moon–Venus–Jupiter conjunction (CC BY 3.0, Pendethan — representative, leads Curiosities); Gion Matsuri (CC BY 2.0, born1945 — representative, leads the Diary). THE LONG READ: "The Eve of Arrival" — anticipation as the productive gap between announcement and arrival, via Tantalus, the Millerite "Great Disappointment" (22 Oct 1844) Le Verrier/Adams' prediction and Galle's discovery of Neptune within ~1° (23 Sep 1846); callbacks to Stevenson (No. 12) Frost (No. 11). Editorial theme: the eve / reach exceeds grasp.

issues.spine: the prepared mind / reserves before the need
issues.title: Dig the Well Before the Thirst
issues.quote: In the fields of observation, chance favours only the prepared mind.
issues.author: Louis Pasteur (lecture, University of Lille, 1854)
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the US–Iran nuclear framework "described in every capital, signed in none" (IAEA's Grossi signals it's close, fresh US oil-smuggling sanctions, Trump's "a few more points"; Iran's negotiator: the winner is whoever is better prepared the day after it's signed) & Brent's nervous retreat to ~US$93–95 (−6% m/m, 6th straight US inventory draw, Chinese imports a 10-yr low, an Oman terminal blast), with Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%) & Ukraine's St Petersburg oil-terminal drone strike as secondaries; SG's S$500 CDC vouchers pulled forward to June on the oil shock (Siow: no blunt across-the-board fuel-duty cut), Q1 GDP revised up to 6% on AI demand, April CPI 1.8%; the SORA-trough refinancing window (3M SORA ~1.08%, flagged closing toward ~1.39% by year-end) & HDB RPI −0.1% Q1 (first dip in ~7 yrs); the H200 licensed for China yet ~undelivered as Beijing steers to Huawei, CFR/Setser noting Huawei's own roadmap trails (no true H200-class part before the Ascend 960, late 2027) & a US AI-power-bill angle, the open-weight reshuffle (GLM-5.1 strongest all-rounder / Kimi K2.6 leads GPQA / DeepSeek V4-Pro long-context) with MiniMax M3 demoted; Oura Ring 5 ships (4 Jun, US$399, blood-pressure "Health Radar") & Kuo's cut-to-two Apple glasses roadmap (Vision Air scrapped) vs Google's audio-first Android XR glasses; Matter 1.5 cameras finally on shelves (CSA "Unify" 16–18 Jun, SmartThings first) & Ubiquiti's UniFi OS 5.1.15 Blueprint engine; Japan "still cheap, quietly cooling" (record 42.7m in 2025, ~−3% in 2026, overtourism management) & the watch-auction barometer (Christie's 10 Jun / Sotheby's "Shapes of Cartier" 15 Jun — results, not previews); the Women's Prize (11 Jun, Choi's Flashlight) & a quiet-arrivals / loud-anticipation culture slate (Toy Story 5, Nolan's Odyssey, Olivia Rodrigo demoted); Family on the evidence toolkit (Nagata/ABCD; monitoring & modelling over reward/punishment; tween 5h33m/day) + the globalising age-gate (Australia's ~4.7m closed child accounts, live AI-chatbot codes) + a "don't be alarmist" box; Whisper's engagement/split season (all flagged); Curiosities on JWST's dawn rock-clouds on WASP-94A b & the lemon-shaped pulsar planet (the prepared instrument; 3I/ATLAS now closed out); Love & Life on company-beats-solitude (Folk & Dunn 2026) & the Harvard study — social capital as a banked reserve; Fitness on banking fast-twitch power (HL-VIRT, Experimental Gerontology 2026) + creatine 3–5g & a longevity-discourse sceptic box; Diary led by the even-year summer matsuri (Sanno 7–17 Jun, Gion, Tenjin, Sumida fireworks) + an SG concert/art slate (BTS demoted to an undated callback). THE LONG READ: "Dig the Well Before the Thirst" — reserves laid down before the moment that demands them, via Joseph's seven-year grain store (Genesis 41), Rome's cura annonae & the horrea granaries, the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (EPCA 1975, after the 1973–74 embargo) & Pasteur's prepared mind (the 1879 chicken-cholera serendipity → attenuated vaccine); callbacks to Frost (No. 11), Stevenson (No. 12) & Franklin (No. 13). Editorial theme: the prepared mind / reserves before the need.

issues.spine: the said and the done
issues.title: The Said and the Done
issues.quote: Well done is better than well said.
issues.author: Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard's Almanack (1737)
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the Hormuz 60-day MOU "described in every capital and signed in none" (Iran suspended talks 1 Jun over Israel's Lebanon push; Hezbollah reportedly accepted a US ceasefire; Trump: deal reachable "over the next week," needs "a few more points") & oil's whipsaw above US$100 then back to ~US$97 Brent (−12% m/m, 6th straight US inventory draw), with Ukraine's drone on Putin's St Petersburg forum (+ Volgograd refinery offline) & Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%) as secondaries; WP's 28 Jun secret-ballot cadres conference over Pritam Singh (account→resign→ballot) & the oil shock reaching the July electricity tariff (29.72c/kWh, sharper hike flagged); the SORA-trough refinancing window (3M SORA ~1%) & June BTO (6,900 flats); the H200 cleared for China yet ~undelivered as Beijing steers to Huawei, the open-weight surge (DeepSeek V4 Pro / Qwen 3.7 Max / Kimi) & frontier-class models now running on desk hardware (DGX Spark, M5 Max, RTX Pro 6000); FUJIKINA & the expected Fujifilm X-T6 (40MP) + Leica's own sensor silicon; Home Assistant local-first (OpenThread BR, native mDNS, Matter sirens); Sotheby's "Shapes of Cartier" 15 Jun & Christie's Patek 3448G "Red Dot"; Olivia Rodrigo's 3rd album (12 Jun) & Taylor Swift's Toy Story 5 single; Family on the age-verification era (Australia under-16, KOSA) + parental-habits-beat-bans + a VPN-spike "don't be alarmist" box; Whisper's engagement/split season (all flagged); Curiosities on JWST's first mid-infrared fingerprint of 3I/ATLAS (the encore) & June's Venus–Jupiter conjunction; Love & Life on relationship quality over status (Folk & Dunn 2026); Fitness on rapamycin possibly blunting exercise gains (Stanfield et al. 2026) & banking VO₂ max early + a sceptic box; Diary led by BTS's National Stadium homecoming & the summer matsuri (even-year Sanno, Gion, Tenjin) + a teamLab art strip. THE LONG READ: "The Said and the Done" — Franklin's maxim on the gap between announcement and execution, via the Kellogg–Briand Pact (1928, war renounced by ~62 signatures with no enforcement), Prohibition / the Volstead Act (1920–33, a ban that manufactured its own evasion → age-gates & VPNs, the cleared-but-unshipped H200) & the Potemkin-village legend (1787, itself likely fabricated — a fake about fakery → vaporware), with the inversion that the week's real deeds (Ukraine's leverage, open weights actually running, the quiet homecomings) outran their words; callbacks to Stevenson (No. 12), Frost (No. 11), Thoreau (No. 10) & Korzybski (No. 09). Editorial theme: the said and the done.

issues.spine: travel hopefully
issues.title: The city that was never there
issues.quote: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive, and the true success is to labour.
issues.author: Robert Louis Stevenson, El Dorado (1881)
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the Hormuz peace "described in every capital and signed in none" (Iran's stalled messaging vs. Rubio's "talks still live") & oil's relief-to-fear whiplash (Brent ~US$95, ~-10% m/m), with Colombia's 21 Jun runoff & Ukraine's oil-infra drone war as secondaries; WP's 28 Jun secret-ballot cadres conference over Pritam Singh & the oil shock in SG tariffs (29.72c/kWh, sharper Q3 hike flagged); HDB RPI's first dip since 2019 (203.4, -0.1% q/q) beside a record 400+ million-dollar flats; the H200 cleared for China yet selling ~nothing as Beijing steers to Huawei Ascend, Anthropic's confidential ~$965B S-1 (no date) topping OpenAI's $852B, MiniMax M3 leading open weights at SWE-Bench Pro ~59%; Sony a7R VI ships (4 Jun) & Sennheiser Momentum 5 (mid-Jun) vs. Fujifilm's first cameraless June; Home Assistant 2026.6 "Pick a card" + two-way IR & Z-Wave lock PINs (legacy template syntax removed); Watches & Wonders' Nautilus-50 & Sotheby's 15 Jun "Shapes of Cartier" vs. the boutique chill; Toy Story 5 / Nolan's all-IMAX Odyssey & the Women's Prize (11 Jun); Family on the age-verification era (Australia under-16, US state laws, KOSA) + a "don't be alarmist" box; Whisper on Hollywood's separation season (all flagged); Curiosities on 3I/ATLAS leaving forever & SETI's Allen-Array silence ("the looking was the win") + JWST-MIRI methanol; Love & Life on relationship quality beating singlehood & the Harvard study; Fitness on VO2 max as the #1 longevity marker & muscle as "magic sauce" + a peptide-hype sceptic box; Diary led by BTS's four-night National Stadium return (first 7-member show in 7 years) & the summer matsuri. THE LONG READ: "The city that was never there" — the things that refuse to arrive (an unsigned peace, a refused chip, a passing comet, a dateless IPO) and why the hopeful travelling toward them is where the living happens, via Stevenson's El Dorado (1881), Ralegh's Manoa/Orinoco hunt (1595/1617), Halley's comet & Le Gentil's two failed transits of Venus (1761/1769); callbacks to Korzybski (No. 09), Thoreau (No. 10) & Frost (No. 11); the one real arrival being BTS's homecoming. Editorial theme: travel hopefully.

issues.spine: through, or around
issues.title: The Toll and the Way Around
issues.quote: The best way out is always through.
issues.author: Robert Frost, A Servant to Servants (1914)
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on Iran suspending the Hormuz talks (1 Jun) & Brent snapping back toward $100 (~-15% m/m), with Colombia's 21 Jun runoff (de la Espriella 43.7% vs Cepeda 40.9%) & Ukraine's St Petersburg oil-terminal strike as secondaries; WP's 28 Jun cadres conference & secret-ballot trigger for Pritam Singh, the oil shock reaching SG electricity tariffs (29.72c/kWh, sharper Jul hike flagged); HDB RPI's first dip since 2019 (203.4, -0.1% q/q); Microsoft Build's own-model turn (MAI-Thinking-1, 35B-active/256k) & Beijing waving away the H200 for Huawei Ascend, MiniMax M3 topping open-weight SWE-Bench Pro at 59.0%; Sony A7R VI (66.8MP) ships & Sennheiser Momentum 5 (16 Jun, screwdriver-replaceable battery); Home Assistant 2026.6 local Z-Wave lock PINs + two-way IR; Watches & Wonders' Nautilus-50 / Hermes H08 Skeleton vs the Gulf luxury chill; Toy Story 5's all-Swift musical & the Women's Prize (11 Jun); Family Desk on the age-gate era (KOSA / App Store Act / Australia under-16 ban) + a "don't be alarmist" box; Curiosities on 3I/ATLAS's colder-sun water & its summer farewell (almost named 3I/Rubin); Love & Life on the dating recession & the Harvard relationships finding; Fitness on muscle-as-index-fund & the VO2-max-overstated sceptic; Diary led by the even-year Sanno Matsuri (7-17 Jun) & BTS's four-night Singapore stand (tickets 5 Jun). THE LONG READ: "The Toll and the Way Around" -- chokepoints & the bypass, via the Oresund Sound Dues (1429-1857, bought out by the 1857 Copenhagen Convention), Vasco da Gama's 1498 Cape route around Venice, & Robert Fortune's 1848 theft of tea; callbacks to Thoreau (No. 10) & Korzybski (No. 09). Editorial theme: through, or around.

issues.spine: the price of anything
issues.title: What's the Quote?
issues.quote: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
issues.author: Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854)
issues.text: Weekend-into-week briefing, 24pp; led on Anthropic's $965B confidential S-1 (1 Jun, narrowly above OpenAI's $852B March mark) \& the Hormuz 60-day MOU returned to Tehran for Trump's third edit (Brent $94.58, −17.4% m/m); Pritam Singh's requisitioned 28 Jun cadre conference with a secret-ballot trigger; the launch of "Screen Smart from the Start" with bescreensmart.gov.sg (only 37% of SG parents confident); HDB Q1 2026 RPI's first dip since 2019 (−0.1% q/q) yet a record 412 $1M flats; Microsoft Build 2026 cuts the OpenAI cord — Project Polaris replaces GPT-4 in Copilot by August, Claude Opus 4.8 \& Sonnet 4.6 land first-party in Azure AI Foundry; MiniMax M3 the first open-weight model to top SWE-Bench Pro at 59.0%; Sony A7R VI ships 4 Jun \& Sennheiser Momentum 5 ships 30 Jun with a screwdriver-replaceable battery; Home Assistant 2026.6 brings Matter onboarding over BLE proxies; Watches \& Wonders centres on Patek's 50th-anniversary Nautilus quartet (2,000-piece 5810/1G) \& the 958G pocket watch; Nolan's $250M all-IMAX-70mm Odyssey + Spielberg's Disclosure Day; Taylor's Version finale (6 Jun); Taiwan Travelogue wins Mandarin's first Booker International; Family Desk on the screen-smart toolkit + APA's gaming risk note; Whisper Desk on Hollywood's separation season (Biggs/Mollen, Daddario/Form confirmed); Curiosities on NASA Goddard's promise of \~100,000 Roman-discovered worlds \& a diamond-core planet; Love \& Life on Tinder's "clear-coding" \& the Wheatley/IFS dating recession; Fitness on the case against over-extending zone 2 (Schoenfeld et al. 2026); Diary led by Sanno Matsuri's even-year procession, Sumida fireworks \& the World Cup opening (11 Jun). THE LONG READ: "What's the Quote?" — Thoreau's cost-of-a-thing anchor pulls three threads (valuation theatre, negotiation as performance, industrialisation of attention) through Newton/South Sea Bubble (1720, Odlyzko on the \~£20,000 loss), Smith's diamond-water paradox (Wealth of Nations, 1776), the Vienna Congress \& Panmunjom armistice as "negotiation under continuous costly action," and Lippmann's Public Opinion (1922, "The World Outside and the Pictures in Our Heads"); callbacks to Korzybski (No. 09) \& Feynman (No. 08). Editorial theme: the price of anything.

issues.title: The Unsigned World
issues.quote: The map is not the territory.
issues.author: Alfred Korzybski
issues.text: Weekend-into-week briefing, 24pp; led on the still-unsigned Hormuz 60-day MOU read five ways (Washington / Tehran / Beijing / Gulf / non-aligned) \& Brent near US$99 (\~17% below a month earlier), with Ukraine's drone-parity turn as the secondary; H200 cleared for China yet booking \~no revenue as Beijing quietly steers firms to Huawei Ascend, DeepSeek V4-Pro's permanent price cut sets a new floor \& the open-weight top-ten goes all-China, SubQ's sub-quadratic LLM; smart-glasses wave (Meta Ray-Ban, Project Aura, Apple's N50 slip), Home Assistant 2026.6 beta \& Ubiquiti's 10-Gig gateways; Watches \& Wonders 2026 (Rolex OP / "100 Years" Rolesor) vs. the Gulf luxury slump; Mandalorian \& Grogu's soft SW opening, "Taiwan Travelogue" Booker; Family on the age-verification era (Australia's under-16 ban as template); Curiosities on 3I/ATLAS hiding in Rubin's pre-discovery frames for ten days; Love \& Life on quality-over-status relationships; Fitness on VO₂ max as a "vital sign" \& exercise snacks; Diary led by the summer matsuri \& teamLab Planets' 2027 close. THE LONG READ: "The Unsigned World" — the gap between map and territory (Korzybski \& Borges's one-to-one map) across the unsigned treaty, the unshipped chip \& the unread comet, via Napoleon's Continental System (1806–14), the 1980s Tanker War / Operation Earnest Will \& Galileo recording Neptune as a "fixed star" (1612–13); callbacks to Feynman (No. 08) \& Proust (No. 07).

issues.quote: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
issues.author: Richard P. Feynman
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 24pp; led on the still-unsigned Hormuz 60-day MOU read differently by each capital \& Brent's \~17% monthly fall; Beijing's all-domestic AI-stack order vs. the H200 in limbo, the West–China inference price gap, SubQ subquadratic LLM; Sony a7R VI / Leica-Gpixel sensor \& Sennheiser Momentum 5, Home Assistant 2026.5; Watches \& Wonders + the Gulf luxury shock; Drake's all-top-3 Billboard sweep; Family on AI companions (Common Sense "unacceptable risk"); Curiosities on Webb imaging a planet's surface \& Rubin's 11,000 asteroids; Fitness on VO₂ max \& the peptide-hype sceptic box; Diary led by BTS's Dec reunion \& the summer matsuri; "the gap between what is written and what is believed" editorial theme (Feynman). FLEX: introduced "The Essay / The Long Read" — a 3-page closing long-form essay ("The Coconut Headphones," cargo-cult science from Feynman's 1974 address, via ELIZA/Weizenbaum, Goodhart's Law, Delphi, Ptolemy \& Galileo) — now a standing fixture (pages 21–23); back cover moved to p.24.

issues.quote: The real voyage of discovery consists not in seeking new landscapes, but in having new eyes.
issues.author: Marcel Proust
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 21pp; led on the 23rd Shangri-La Dialogue (a milder Hegseth, China sending only scholars) \& the still-unsigned Hormuz 60-day MOU across five viewpoint panels; open-weight pack ties the frontier (Kimi K2.6 / MiMo 54), Singapore EC overhaul (MOP 5→10yr), Sony 1000X ColleXion vs Sennheiser Momentum 5, Home Assistant native IR+RF, Taiwan Travelogue's Booker; Curiosities on 3I/ATLAS's "alien water" \& the Rubin deluge; "new instruments, old frictions" editorial theme.

issues.quote: Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.
issues.author: Carl Sagan
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 21pp; led on the unsigned Hormuz 60-day MOU (Trump's "final determination"), Brent's \~17% monthly fall \& the Galați drone (28th NATO breach); chip-ban reversal vs. China self-sufficiency, five open-weight frontier models in 30 days, Sony A7R VI, Oyster centennial \& the Birkin index, interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS; "desk \& the dark" editorial theme.

issues.quote: It is the mark of an educated mind to be able to entertain a thought without accepting it.
issues.author: Aristotle
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 21pp; led on the Hormuz 60-day MOU framework, the 23rd Shangri-La Dialogue \& Ukraine drone-war turning; Cannes Palme to Mungiu's Fjord, Drake's triple-drop, "Taiwan Travelogue" first Mandarin Booker; multi-viewpoint editorial theme.

issues.quote: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
issues.author: Marie Curie
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 21pp; led on the Hormuz ceasefire framework \& Shangri-La Dialogue; Nvidia "evacuating" China; full twelve-desk skeleton.

issues.quote: Peace cannot be kept by force; it can only be achieved by understanding.
issues.author: Albert Einstein
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 21pp; led on the 2026 Iran war \& Hormuz oil shock; full twelve-desk skeleton.

issues.quote: The future is already here — it's just not very evenly distributed.
issues.author: William Gibson
issues.text: Weekend Edition, 21pp; added The Kit, Connected Home, Family Desk, Fitness \& The Diary.

issues.quote: A good briefing tells you what happened. A great one tells you what people are arguing about.
issues.author: House line
issues.text: First edition (daily format, 14pp); pre-tagline.
